commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Keep norm layers neutral under dummy weight init
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep normalization layers neutral under `--load-format dummy`: `RMSNorm`, `LayerNorm`, `RMSNormGated` and `GemmaRMSNorm` tag their parameters with `dummy_weight_value` (their identity value), so dummy init no longer fills them with ±1e-3. Follow-up to #61134 (dtype-aware dummy init).

## Claims

- Dummy-loaded norms are identity-like (weight 1, bias 0; Gemma's `1 + w` weight 0) instead of random ±1e-3.
- Activations then keep a realistic scale, so data-dependent kernels time like they do with real weights. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, the sparse indexer's `topKPerRowPrefill` takes 27.8 ms per forward with dummy weights on `main`, 10.7 ms with this PR, and 10.6 ms with real weights.
- Only dummy initialization changes; checkpoint loading is unaffected.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (40 layers), TP4 + EP on 4x GB200, MegaMoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, MXFP4 indexer cache. One prefill step: 8 requests x 1024 new tokens at ~100K context each. GPU kernel time per forward from a profiled CUDA-graph replay of the model forward (3 replays):

| Weights | `topKPerRowPrefill` (ms/forward) | Forward (ms, median of 100 replays) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dummy, `main` (norms ±1e-3) | 27.84 | 136.0 |
| dummy, this PR | 10.68 | 120.3 |
| real checkpoint | 10.64 | 124.1 |

The remaining forward gap to real weights is MoE routing (real routing from random token IDs vs. a balanced fixture), not this change. All other kernels differ by under 1 ms between this PR and real weights.

These numbers come from an exact-shape forward benchmark that isn't upstream yet; the per-kernel effect can also be seen in an `nsys` profile of any long-context DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill with `--load-format dummy`.

Unit test (in `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`):

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -q
43 passed
```

`test_dummy_norm_weights_are_neutral` fails on `main` (`RMSNorm` weight stays random) and passes with this PR.

No model evaluation: only `--load-format dummy` values change.

## Details

- **Root cause.** With norm weights in ±1e-3, every normalized sublayer input shrinks by ~1000x and loses structure. DeepSeek-V4.1's indexer query ends up near zero, and after FP8/MXFP4 quantization its logits collapse onto a few values with many exact ties. `topKPerRowPrefill` is a data-dependent radix select, so these degenerate logits are its slow case; real models never produce them.
- **Mechanism.** Reuses the existing `dummy_weight_value` hook in `initialize_single_dummy_weight`, as DeepSeek-V4.1's engram already does for its own weights. Each norm declares the value its constructor already uses.
- **Limitation.** Model-local norm classes that don't build on these four layers keep random dummy values.
- **Behavior change.** Dummy-weight benchmarks of models with data-dependent kernels (sparse top-k, etc.) shift toward their real-weight timings.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't split a multimodal item that a prefill chunk starts exactly on
commits.pr_body:
FIX #52306

## Purpose

Under `disable_chunked_mm_input=True` the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when the chunk begins exactly on it.

`_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` guards the split with

```python
self.scheduler_config.disable_chunked_mm_input
and num_computed_tokens < start_pos                                            # (A)
and (num_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens) < (start_pos + num_encoder_tokens)  # (B)
```

(A) is false when `num_computed_tokens == start_pos`, so (B) never runs and a chunk too small to cover the item is allowed through. That equality is not an exotic state — it is exactly what the guard itself produces: the rollback sets `num_new_tokens = start_pos - num_computed_tokens`, so the next step starts on the item. If the budget cannot fit the whole item on that step, the item is split at the precise point the flag exists to prevent. For models with bidirectional attention over the item, the tokens that should cross-attend silently cannot.

The fix is `<=` in (A). Only the equality case changes:

- `num_computed_tokens < start_pos` — unchanged, rolls back to just before the item.
- `num_computed_tokens == start_pos` and the chunk does not cover the item — now yields `num_new_tokens = 0`, so the request waits for a step that can fit it. This matches the neighbouring `can_allocate` branch, which already returns 0 rather than scheduling a partial item.
- `num_computed_tokens > start_pos` (prefix caching landing mid-item) — unchanged.

Returning 0 cannot starve the request: `_verify_args` already rejects a `max_num_batched_tokens` smaller than the longest multimodal item when this flag is set (`test_no_mm_input_chunking` asserts that `ValueError`), so a step that can fit the item always exists.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_no_mm_input_chunking_at_item_boundary` drives `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` on a real scheduler and request (mm item at offset 400, length 800) across the three cases: starting before the item, starting on it without room, and starting on it with room. The existing `test_no_mm_input_chunking` only exercises the first, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Test Result

I have no GPU or vLLM build on this machine, so I could not execute the suite — that run is CI's, and I will follow it. What I verified locally: the condition and the surrounding branches on current `main`, the neighbouring `can_allocate` handling that this now matches, and the `max_num_batched_tokens` validation that rules out starvation. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both files.

The reporter's direct-call reproduction on unpatched `main` shows the failure this fixes:

```
print(ask(0, 500))    # 3    - correct, stops before the item
print(ask(3, 500))    # 500  - wrong, splits the 766-token item
```

## Contribution notes (per `AGENTS.md`)

- Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52306 in:body"` and `--search "disable_chunked_mm_input"` return nothing; the issue has no linked PR.
- Not model-affecting in the eval sense (a scheduling boundary), so no eval numbers apply — though the user-visible symptom is degraded output for bidirectional-attention multimodal models, which is why the regression test asserts the boundary directly.
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change. I read every changed line, checked the branch behaviour against `main` myself, and can defend it. The judgement call worth a reviewer's eye: the equality case now returns 0 rather than a partial schedule, which costs one scheduling step in exchange for never splitting the item.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Fuse DeepEP-v2 decode globalize+align into one launch
commits.pr_body:
Fuses the DeepEP-v2 INDEXED cudagraph-decode metadata chain (`_globalize_recv_topk_idx` + `moe_align_block_size` + `count_and_sort_expert_tokens`) into a single CUDA launch for the Humming path.

`recv_topk_idx` holds **local** expert ids; the kernel bins by local id (align/sort) while writing back the global id, and reads `num_recv` on-device from `psum[-1]` so it is CUDA-graph safe. Sizing by local (not global) experts shrinks the sentinel/`expert_ids` region by ~`ep_size` under EP. The fused kernel also produces the optional scatter index used by Humming for larger EP batches.

The fused path is selected for CUDA Humming INDEXED experts when DeepEP-v2 defers globalization during CUDA-graph decode. Other paths keep the standalone globalization and alignment behavior.

## Numbers

H200, EP32, INDEXED decode — fused vs the 3-kernel chain, measured before the October 6 rebase:

| tokens | speedup |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1.23x |
| 8 | 1.14x |
| 32 | 1.16x |
| 64 | 1.36x |
| 128 | 1.67x |
| 256 (n=8192) | 2.01x |

## Testing

After the October 12 rebase onto upstream commit `c599b5971`: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the six changed Python files; Apple `clang-format` 21 `--dry-run --Werror` passed on the changed CUDA/C++ files; `git diff --check` passed. `git range-diff` confirmed that the functional patch is unchanged apart from adapting paths to upstream's new `csrc/moe` layout. CI then found a stale `libtorch_stable/torch_utils.h` include in the moved CUDA source; commit `52d7e1c15` changes it to `torch_utils.h`, matching the other MoE CUDA files. The corrected include and formatting were checked locally, but the CUDA build needs to rerun in CI. The pinned `clang-format` and mypy hooks passed on the prior October 7 base but were not rerun here. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_globalize_align_block_size.py -v` could not run on the macOS rebase host. The test includes correctness cases for the optional scatter index.

Pending on CUDA hardware: `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuild, the pytest run, and a model evaluation (for example gsm8k) with the fused path active. The kernel originated from a validated standalone prototype; the measurements above have not been repeated on the rebased code.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate — no open PR fused this chain when the PR was created (`gh pr list --search "globalize align"`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) was used. Human review of the rebase resolution and GPU validation are pending.

commits.pr_title: [ROCM][Bugfix] Deferring to TRITON_ATTN backend for Prefix lm models instead of ROCM_ATTN and fixed minor bug in Gemma3 Multimodal code
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes incorrect attention behavior for prefix-LM multimodal models (e.g., Gemma3) on ROCm. This is a correctness fix. 

**Root cause:** Both `RocmAttentionBackend` and `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend` overrode
`supports_mm_prefix()` to return `True`, but neither backend actually implements the
`mm_prefix_range_tensor` passing required for bidirectional image-token attention during prefill. As a result,
prefix-LM multimodal models on ROCm were silently falling through with wrong attention masks and
image tokens were not attending to each other bidirectionally as required by models like Gemma3.

**Changes:**
1. **`rocm_attn.py` / `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`**: Removed the incorrect
   `supports_mm_prefix() -> True` overrides. Both backends now inherit the base-class default
   (`False`), causing the attention backend selector to correctly defer to Triton unified
   attention for prefix-LM models on ROCm.
2. **`gemma3_mm.py`**: Explicitly sets `config.text_config.is_mm_prefix_lm = True` in the
   multimodal constructor, since the text-only Gemma3 path does not set this flag but the
   multimodal path requires it for correct image-token attention.
3. **`rocm.py`**: Ports the `disable_chunked_mm_input` guard from the CUDA platform path to
   ROCm. For prefix-LM multimodal models, chunked prefill can split a multimodal item and
   break the intended bidirectional attention pattern; this ensures ROCm disables it
   automatically, matching CUDA behavior.
4. **`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py`**: Adds a regression test
   asserting that both ROCm backends do not claim `mm_prefix` support, guarding against this
   being re-introduced silently.

## Test Plan

**Unit test (ROCm):**
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py \
  -v -k test_rocm_backends_do_not_support_mm_prefix
```

```bash
    --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \
    --batch_size 16

# 12B

    --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \

```

Multimodal task - `MMMU-val`:

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run the Clef pooler test on GPU
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Run `tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_clef_omni.py` (added in #61064) on the GPU. As a CPU test it broke engine startup for every later test in the multimodal pooling shard.

## Claims

- Fixes `CUDA error: initialization error` at engine startup for the tests after `test_clef_omni.py` in `pytest models/multimodal/pooling -m 'not core_model'` (clip, colmodernvbert, colpali, colqwen3: 3 failed + 22 errors locally).
- Test-only change; no runtime code is touched.

## Validation

Reproducer — the clef test followed by any engine test in one pytest process:

```bash
cd tests
pytest -q models/multimodal/pooling/test_clef_omni.py \
  "models/multimodal/pooling/test_clip.py::test_models[float-openai/clip-vit-base-patch32]"
```

| | Result (GB200) |
|---|---|
| `main` | `1 failed, 1 passed` — EngineCore: `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: initialization error` |
| This PR | `2 passed`; vLLM now logs "We must use the `spawn` multiprocessing start method" |

- `test_clef_omni.py` alone passes repeatedly on GPU with the original tolerances (`atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4`).
- Full shard `pytest -v -s models/multimodal/pooling -m 'not core_model'` with this change: clip, colmodernvbert, colpali, and all 18 colqwen3 cases pass; no `initialization error` remains. Remaining local failures are unrelated and also fail standalone on `main`: `test_colpali_v2_multimodal_text_query_image_docs` (forced `FLASH_ATTN` rejects the block size on GB200) and three `test_embedding_gemma2.py` unit tests (local transformers lacks `embedding_gemma2`).

## Details

Root cause: the test fed CPU tensors through `PoolingMetadata.build_pooling_cursor` and `JointSchemaPooler`, both of which allocate pinned host memory (`pin_memory=PIN_MEMORY`, `async_tensor_h2d`). Pinning creates a CUDA context in the pytest process without going through torch's lazy init, so `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` stays `False`. `_maybe_force_spawn` therefore keeps `fork`, and the forked EngineCore fails to initialize CUDA. The shard only recovered once a later test (`test_colqwen3_5.py`) initialized CUDA through torch, flipping vLLM to `spawn`.

This test only runs in the GPU "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step, so running it on `current_platform.device_type` matches the directory and production (`hidden_states.device`), and CUDA is initialized through torch so vLLM correctly picks `spawn`. Alternatives considered: skipping pinning for CPU targets in `build_pooling_cursor` (touches shared runtime code for a test-only issue, and the pooler's `async_tensor_h2d` would still pin), or forcing `spawn` for the whole shard (slower, and hides the cause).

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `test_clef_omni.py` or this failure.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Add lifecycle hooks for worker extensions
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Related to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59120. Worker extensions currently require callers to initialize their state manually. This change adds optional `init_worker_extension()` and `destroy_worker_extension()` hooks: initialization runs after device and distributed setup, and cleanup runs before worker shutdown. Hooks are selected from the configured extension class, so a previously injected extension cannot be called by mistake. Ray executors currently force-kill worker actors, so cleanup is not guaranteed on Ray shutdown.

Currently the implementation is a rough initial draft. Will need further discussion in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59120.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and review.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] per_token_group_quant_8bit: multiply by reciprocal instead of dividing per element
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Speed up FP8 per-token-group quantization by computing the per-group scale reciprocal once and multiplying, instead of dividing per element. This covers both CUDA group-quant kernels: `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (smem and register-resident schedules) and the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`), so that all CUDA fp8 group-quant paths share the same reciprocal-multiply numerics. ~1.2-1.3x kernel speedup on GB300 across M=1..32768; ~1-2% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP4).

## Claims

- 1.15-1.29x faster `per_token_group_fp8_quant` CUDA kernel on GB300 across M=1..32768 (details below).
- All CUDA fp8 group-quant paths (unfused kernel, fused RMSNorm+quant kernel, Triton fallback, UE8M0 path) now use the same reciprocal-multiply numerics; previously the fused and unfused kernels could disagree by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements.
- ~0.6-2.0% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, at concurrency 1-64.
- Accuracy-neutral: GSM8K / GPQA-Diamond deltas within noise (details below).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`: 848 passed, including `test_per_token_group_quant_fp8_register_matches_smem` (bitwise register-vs-smem equality; both schedules are changed identically, so the invariant is preserved).
- Scale outputs are bit-identical to main; quantized values can differ by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (randn data) when a quotient lands within 1 fp32 ulp of an fp8 rounding boundary.

### Microbenchmarks

GB300, K=4096, group=128, bf16 -> fp8e4m3 + fp32 scales. FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graph and cold L2; median of interleaved rounds. Both columns are standalone same-toolchain builds (nvcc 13.1) of the register-resident kernel; repro harness: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_per_token_group_quant.py`.

| M | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup | achieved BW (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.30 | 1.92 | 1.20x | 6 GB/s |
| 4 | 2.34 | 1.92 | 1.22x | 26 GB/s |
| 16 | 2.56 | 2.14 | 1.20x | 93 GB/s |
| 64 | 2.69 | 2.27 | 1.19x | 350 GB/s |
| 256 | 3.20 | 2.78 | 1.15x | 1.14 TB/s |
| 1024 | 6.14 | 5.02 | 1.22x | 2.53 TB/s |
| 4096 | 15.23 | 12.19 | 1.25x | 4.17 TB/s |
| 16384 | 52.35 | 41.09 | 1.27x | 4.95 TB/s |
| 32768 | 101.25 | 78.34 | 1.29x | 5.19 TB/s |

The kernel is memory-bound (~2 FLOPs/element; TFLOPS is not the meaningful metric here). This PR lifts achieved bandwidth from 4.0 to 5.2 TB/s at M=32768. A flat-index Triton variant we prototyped reaches 6.7 TB/s at M=32768 but loses at small M; modifying the existing CUDA kernel is the lower-risk change.

### E2E perf

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, vllm bench serve; median TPOT. main (`c077dc663d`) and the branch (`1aca0a263f`) ran sequentially on the same GB300 node:

| Concurrency | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.27 | 6.23 | -0.6% |
| 4 | 8.30 | 8.14 | -1.9% |
| 16 | 12.06 | 11.82 | -2.0% |
| 64 | 24.98 | 24.67 | -1.2% |

Request throughput +1.2% at concurrency 64. Note: the e2e delta includes a toolchain effect (branch built from source with local nvcc 13.1; baseline is the nvcc 13.0 wheel, whose stock quant kernel is mis-scheduled -- see Details), so it mildly overstates the pure source-change effect. The same-toolchain kernel numbers above are the honest claim.

### Accuracy

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, identical server flags on the same GB300 node:

| Task | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K flexible-extract (n=1319) | 0.8211 | 0.8112 | -0.99pp |
| GSM8K strict-match (n=1319) | 0.8158 | 0.7991 | -1.67pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (n=198) | 0.8586 | 0.8687 | +1.01pp |

Mixed and within noise (binomial std error ~1.06pp per arm at n=1319), but GSM8K drifts down directionally; consistent with the ~0.05% of elements whose fp8 rounding flips under reciprocal-multiply.

## Details

- Root cause: `div.rn.f32` is a multi-instruction slow sequence, and the kernel issued it once per *element* when one division per *group* suffices. The kernel's own UE8M0 path already uses reciprocal-multiply (a power-of-two scale makes the reciprocal exact); this PR applies the same transform to the fp32-scale path.
- The per-element division was inherited from the SGLang kernel this file was ported from (#21083); the register-resident path (#55330) kept it so the new schedule stayed bit-exact with the smem one. That invariant is a test convenience, not an accuracy requirement, and is preserved by changing both schedules identically.
- Numerics: this is the same rcp-mul numerics class already shipped by this kernel's UE8M0 path, vLLM's Triton fallback (`_per_token_group_quant_fp8`), and SGLang's production quant kernel.
- Scope: no Python/dispatch changes. The file is also hipified into ROCm builds; the change uses only portable float ops, so ROCm gets the same numerics (not separately benchmarked there).
- Related work: #60903 adds a separate Triton row kernel for prefill-sized inputs (large M only); this PR instead speeds up the existing CUDA kernel at all M and is complementary. No open PR duplicates this change.
- Consistency: the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`, the target of `RMSNormQuantFusionPass` for block-FP8 models, on both CUDA and ROCm via hipify) is switched to the same reciprocal-multiply. Without this, fused and unfused paths diverge by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (caught by `test_fused_quant_layernorm` and `test_mamba_prefix_cache`). The fused kernel also drops 4 div.rn per vec4. Per-token fp8 keeps exact per-element division for FBGemm parity; int8 paths are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Toolchain note: nvcc 13.0 x sm_100 mis-schedules the stock kernel</summary>

All official artifacts (release pipeline nvcc 13.0.2, Dockerfile CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3) target `... 10.0 ...` (no sm_103). nvcc 13.0 targeting sm_100 mis-schedules this kernel's div.rn slow paths: 864 instructions / 3095 static stall cycles vs 568 / 1655 under nvcc 13.1; the shipped wheel runs the stock kernel at 167.6us vs 101.2us for a 13.1 rebuild at M=32768 (sm_100 SASS loads natively on sm_103; verified with CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1). This PR's variant is insensitive to the compiler (78.3us on nvcc 13.0 vs 78.1us on 13.1) because it removes the per-element div.rn entirely. Worth a separate build-toolchain discussion; out of scope here.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Enable FA4 sparse MQA decode on Blackwell
commits.pr_body:
[Attention] Enable FA4 sparse MQA decode on Blackwell

This adds `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4`, a sparse MLA backend for Blackwell with a BF16 KV cache. The FA4 CuTe DSL kernel from vllm-project/flash-attention#195 serves decode batches and the decode rows of mixed HiSparse batches. Every other batch runs on the trtllm-gen lane, as in `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`. At 16 or fewer query heads per rank the backend is the first choice, with and without HiSparse; above that head count it stays opt-in.

The first commit, "Share sparse MLA MQA cache handling", will go up as its own PR and is only here until it lands. It moves index conversion and the HiSparse lane split from the FA3 and FlashInfer sparse MLA backends into `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mqa`, so a backend implements only `_forward_mqa_kernel(..., is_decode)`. The design is by @LucasWilkinson. One FA3 behaviour changes with it: FA3's plain path converts top-k through the index group's shared buffer, as FlashInfer already did, instead of once per layer. The values are identical while the layers of a group share block stride, block table and request ids, which index groups guarantee. A test pins leader and follower layers.

The second commit is the FA4 backend on top of that hook:

- `flash_attn_varlen_func` forwards `gather_kv_indices`, `gather_kv_valid_length` and `q_v` to FA4.
- The impl subclasses `FlashInferMLASparseImpl`. Its hook runs the FA4 decode kernel when `is_decode`, otherwise FlashInfer's trtllm-gen call with the LSE converted to base e.
- The metadata builder subclasses the FlashInfer TRTLLM builder and declares `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graph support. Inheriting the builder brings the DCP workspace pre-size: an earlier version of this PR used the default 394 MiB trtllm workspace on its prefill lane and crashed under DCP 2 on a prefill step of about 8192 tokens, where the softmax-stats slab needs 513 MiB.
- The backend class subclasses the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend for its gates (PCP with DCP rejected, head dims) and adds the FA4 gates: `index_topk` a multiple of 128, and a supported gathered head count under DCP.
- Under HiSparse, decode reads the hot buffer through the shared lanes. The inherited `autotune_hisparse_decode` compiles the FA4 kernel before graph capture.
- FA4 shares FlashInfer's masked-MHA thresholds.
- FA4 joins `_uses_flat_kv_cache`, since it reads the same flat KV cache as FlashInfer.

The last commit bumps the flash-attention pin to vllm-project/flash-attention 2e3a6694, which has #195 and the sparse decode split-rule tuning for DCP shapes (vllm-project/flash-attention#200).

## Performance

GLM-5.2 NVFP4-FP8 with BF16 KV on B300, TP4, FA4 against `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` from the same tree (this PR on `main` d71f662606), change in median ITL (negative favours FA4). Plain and DCP 2 are averaged over two runs. The HiSparse column assumes #59309 is merged: it applies that PR's diff, pins the MoE autotune tactics so both backends run the same MoE kernels, and averages two server starts with two runs each.

| Input / concurrency / output | TP4 plain | TP4 DCP 2 | TP4 HiSparse |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 8 / 256 | -4.2% | -6.7% | -0.8% |
| 4096 / 128 / 256 | -4.3% | -2.3% | +1.3%* |
| 32768 / 16 / 256 | -5.3% | -5.1% | +0.2% |

\* One FA4 run measured 35.2 ms against 33.4 to 33.7 ms for the other three; without it the figure is +0.1%.

Under HiSparse FA4 is on par with FlashInfer, which did not justify a separate priority order. Per decode step, FA4's attention kernels take about 190 µs less than FlashInfer's at 4096 / 8, but start-to-start variance in all-reduce time is larger than that difference. On current `main`, #59235 makes HiSparse about 0.45 ms per decode step slower for both backends, because it writes `request_ids` in every layer. #59309 moves those writes into the group leader's resolve, which brings the 57 follower layers' 171 kernels per step back out of the decode graph.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 475 passed, 672 skipped. `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 5 passed (FlashInfer and FA4). The FlashInfer, KV cache layout, backend selection and masked-MHA routing tests pass as well.
- Serving, GLM-5.2 NVFP4-FP8, TP4, HiSparse, GSM8K (500 questions, 5-shot): FA4 0.936, FA4 with MTP 0.948, FlashInfer 0.946. No invalid responses; 8K, 16K and 30K needle prompts answered correctly.
- FlashInfer on the shared base: latency within noise of `main`, plain generations byte-identical.
- The FA3 sparse backend did not run on hardware here (SM90 kernel, SM100 machine); its change is covered by unit tests only.

AI-assisted. The September 7 upstream search found no matching open FA4 sparse-MLA integration PR; related platform-specific work does not provide this SM100 backend.

commits.pr_title: [MoRIIO] Require pending remote prefill for READ cache hits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MoRIIO READ can claim external cache hits for a request with no pending remote prefill, even though allocation will not schedule a READ. Require `do_remote_prefill` before reporting a READ hit.

Rebased onto main `bfa7e5b7afe40ebe48288801a2baf5c1135cd881`. This remains an independent child of closed #58968.

## Claims

```diff
D receives a request without pending remote prefill
- MoRIIO reports an external hit; no matching READ is scheduled
+ MoRIIO reports zero; local computation or another connector can serve it
```

The eligible READ path retains N−1 accounting and synchronous loading. Producer and WRITE behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Validated on `89e3abbb7133a4b340e67b882c0eb9cb710ef402` (2026-10-12): **99 passed, 32 ROCm-only skips**. Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy for Python 3.11 and test/CI tethering checks.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -ra \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py
```

Fresh negative control on current main: absent, empty and false remote-prefill parameters incorrectly return `(31, False)` for a 32-token READ request (**3 failed, 1 passing control**). The four cases pass here. READ and WRITE now share the existing eligibility guard from merged #53250; WRITE semantics and N−1 READ accounting are preserved. This also avoids a rebase-induced optional/non-optional assignment error caught by mypy.

The additional connector suite is skipped by its ROCm/aiter requirement in the CPU environment. Historical MoRIIO+LMCache recovery exposed the false hit, but exact-source serving/RDMA validation remains pending; subsequent NaNs were not attributed to this guard.

The eight independent PRs compose on this same main. The combined CPU suite passes **344 tests**, with **33 skips** (32 ROCm/aiter-gated connector cases and one GPU LLM case) and **one model-loading deselection**. Counts overlap with the independent suites.

## Details

`get_num_new_matched_tokens` shares one remote-prefill guard across READ and WRITE, matching the eligibility flag used by `update_state_after_alloc`. Existing READ fixtures explicitly set that flag; the regression reuses the scheduler suite's fixture.

Duplicate checks: #53250 and #60544 add eligibility in WRITE, #54301 changes READ to an asynchronous lifecycle, and #48471 adjusts block-list matching. None supplies this READ-only eligibility guard. The matching implementation in #58968 was superseded by the split PRs.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; blast radius: MoRIIO READ admission. No base connector API or KV transfer clipping change.

Merged #53250 supplies WRITE eligibility; this extends its existing guard to READ. #60867 changes group routing and speculation gates, not this admission check.

AI assistance was used for implementation, rebase, regression checks and this description. Human line-by-line review and the runtime acceptance items above remain pending. No performance improvement is claimed.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Warm up DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernels before serving
commits.pr_body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepGEMM warmup covers `fp8_gemm_nt` and the grouped MoE GEMM. It does not cover `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` or the `bf16_mega_gate` that routes into it. With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 therefore JIT-compile these kernels on the first request at each new prefill size. This PR adds them to `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, following the structure of the two existing DeepGEMM warmups there.

## Claims

- No serving-time compiles of the MegaMoE kernels: `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, `bf16_mega_gate` and the Triton input-staging kernel. Before: 60 DeepGEMM compiles in one DeepSeek-V4 benchmark run. For Kimi K3, the 2 SiTU `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` compiles during serving that cost 2.6-2.9 s of TTFT each go to 0, at about +10 s of startup.
- MTP speculative decoding needs nothing extra. The DeepSeek-V4 MTP drafter's MegaMoE layer uses the same kernels as the target's, and there were 0 DeepGEMM compiles during serving with MTP on.
- DeepSeek-V4: the first request at a new prefill size no longer stalls for 3.5 to 6 s. It now takes about the same time as a repeat. The exception is a one-time 60-85 ms communication-buffer setup on the server's first large prefill, which is not a compile (see Details).
- Cost: for DeepSeek-V4, the first startup on a cold DeepGEMM cache takes about 4 to 5 min longer (+247 to +299 s on fully empty caches). A warm restart takes the same time as before. For Kimi K3, it is about +10 s.

## Validation

**Setup (DeepSeek-V4).** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x B300, TP2 + EP2, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, `--max-model-len 16384`, prefix caching off, Model Runner V2. vLLM precompiled wheel `3ca00a82` (cu130) with its bundled DeepGEMM.

Each run used a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` seeded with every non-mega DeepGEMM kernel, so only the mega kernels start cold.

**Workload.** One request at a time: token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`, `max_tokens` 4, streamed time to first token (TTFT).
1. Six fixed lengths (100 to 8000 tokens). Each gets a first request, then 3 repeats with new random tokens.
2. 40 seeded random lengths from 51 to 15504 tokens. The warmup did not pick these.
3. 32 concurrent requests.

**JIT compiles during serving.** Counted as new entries in the DeepGEMM cache dir between "Application startup complete" and the end of the workload, across all kernel families. Triton, CuTeDSL and TileLang compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` | 58 | 0 |
| `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | 2 | 0 |
| other DeepGEMM families | 0 | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` | ≥1 (see note) | 0 |

On main, the Triton row comes from the default (non-verbose) JIT monitor, which logs only the first compile per kernel, so the true count is unknown. The previous revision of this PR, which warmed without a padding mask, compiled 3 variants for just three prompt lengths in a verbose run.

A separate single-GPU check called both kernels for every per-rank token count from 1 to 8192 after the warmup's representative sizes. It produced 0 new cache entries. An independent rerun of the patched server, with 20 prompt lengths, 16 of them chosen to give unaligned per-rank chunks, saw 0 JIT events.

**TTFT, first request vs median of 3 repeats (ms):**

| prompt tokens | main, first | main, repeat | this PR, first | this PR, repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| 2000 | 3503 | 106 | 112 | 103 |
| 4000 | 5913 | 119 | 178 | 117 |
| 8000 | 3489 | 136 | 141 | 136 |

- 40 random lengths: 24 of the 40 requests on main took 3.5 to 6.0 s. The slowest on this PR took 0.27 s. Total TTFT went from 90.1 s to 6.1 s.
- 32 concurrent requests: worst TTFT went from 8.33 s to 1.47 s.

**Startup, `init engine` (profile, KV cache, warmup, graph capture):**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold mega-kernel cache (all other kernels cached) | 141 s | 428 s |
| fully empty caches, no MTP (separate tester run) | 444 s | 691 s (+247 s) |
| fully empty caches, with MTP (separate tester run) | 406 s | 705 s (+299 s) |
| warm restart, same cache dir | 63 s | 63 s |

KV cache sizing is unchanged: 163.13 GiB and 465,145 tokens in both.

**MTP (DeepSeek-V4, `--speculative_config.method=mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2`, same setup and workload):**

| MegaMoE compiles during serving | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| seeded cache (mega kernels cold), 1 run | not run | 0 |
| fully empty caches, 1 run (separate tester) | 2 `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, 10 `bf16_mega_gate`, 6 Triton staging | 0 |

On this PR's commit with MTP: the server was healthy, GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) scored 0.970, and mean MTP acceptance length was 2.62 on GSM8K. On the random-token benchmark, acceptance was 1.61, against 1.55 on the previous revision. DeepGEMM compiles during serving: 0.

The drafter needs no extra warmup. Its MegaMoE layer reuses the target's kernels, and the tester's tracer saw no DeepGEMM compile in the drafter during serving on either build.

**Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, a pruned checkpoint):** 4x B300, TP4 + EP4 with sequence parallelism, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192 (2048 per rank), fp8 KV, no prefix caching, no spec decode.
- Each run started with empty DeepGEMM, Triton, Inductor and vLLM caches. One run per build.
- Workload: one 3000-token request, a second 3000-token request with new tokens, then 137, 1500, 5000 and 8000 tokens.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepGEMM compiles during serving | 2 (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` SiTU, `block_m` 128 and 192) | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` compiled during serving | yes (ranks 1-3, first request) | no |
| TTFT at 1500 / 5000 tokens | 2734 / 3139 ms | 153 / 244 ms |
| `init engine` | 46 s* | 56-57 s |

\*The main run had a warm FlashInfer JIT cache from an earlier run. The PR runs had one too, so the +10 s compares like with like.

On both builds, two non-MegaMoE kernels still compile during serving: the Inductor kernel `triton_poi_fused_mul_sigmoid_0`, on the first prefill above the capture sizes, and the KDA gated RMSNorm Triton kernel `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`. They are outside this PR.

**Fully cold cache.** With every DeepGEMM and Triton cache empty (not just the mega kernels), three other DeepGEMM kernel families still compile on first use with this PR. They are outside MegaMoE and left for follow-ups:
- `fp8_einsum` in `o_proj` (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`): 2 kernels.
- `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`: 8 kernels without MTP, 6 with MTP.
- The sparse indexer's `sm100_mqa_logits`: 1 kernel.

With MTP, the spec-decode rejection-sampler Triton kernels also compile on first use on both builds. That is unrelated to this PR.

**Tests.** `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` adds two CPU tests:
- The layer predicate is False for other models, and neither model module is imported. It is True only for DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MegaMoE layers.
- The warmup sizes for each `bf16_mega_gate` config are above the gate's token threshold, so the forward reaches the kernel.

All 8 tests pass.

**CI gap.** This path needs SM100 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4 or Kimi K3 with the native MegaMoE backend, and expert parallelism. CI has no such setup, so the validation above was run by hand.

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

```bash
# server (baseline: same command on main)
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8234

# client: fixed lengths x (1 first + 3 repeats), 40 random lengths, 32-request burst;
# records TTFT and the new DeepGEMM cache entries per request
SWEEP=40 python bench.py 8234 $DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR results.json
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""First-hit benchmark. Phase 1 (fixed): for each prompt length, one request
at a time: a first hit, then REPEATS more with fresh random tokens. Phase 2
(sweep, optional): random lengths the warmup did not pick, then a concurrent
burst (mixed prefill + decode). Records TTFT and every DeepGEMM JIT cache
entry created during serving, per kernel family."""
import collections, concurrent.futures as cf, json, os, random, re, sys, time
import requests

port, dgdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
LENGTHS = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("LENGTHS", "100,400,1000,2000,4000,8000").split(",")]
REPEATS = int(os.environ.get("REPEATS", "3"))
SWEEP = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP", "0"))
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
cache = os.path.join(dgdir, "cache")

def entries():
    return set(os.listdir(cache))

def family(e):
    m = re.match(r"(?:kernel\.)?(.+?)\.[0-9a-f]{32}$", e)
    return m.group(1) if m else e

def fam_count(es):
    return dict(collections.Counter(family(e) for e in es))

def ttft(prompt_ids, max_tokens=4):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(URL, json=dict(model=MODEL, prompt=prompt_ids, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                     temperature=0, stream=True, ignore_eos=True),
                      stream=True, timeout=3600)
    first = None
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line and line.startswith(b"data: ") and line != b"data: [DONE]" and first is None:
            first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return first, time.perf_counter() - t0

rng = random.Random(0)
def prompt(L):
    return [rng.randrange(1000, 100000) for _ in range(L)]

start = entries()
print(f"entries at ready: {len(start)} {fam_count(start)}", flush=True)
rows = []
ttft(prompt(8))  # HTTP/tokenizer warm; 4 per-rank tokens -> no mega gate
for L in LENGTHS:
    for i in range(1 + REPEATS):
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        new = entries() - before
        rows.append(dict(phase="fixed", prompt_len=L, rep="first" if i == 0 else f"repeat{i}",
                         ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e, new=fam_count(new)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
after_fixed = entries()
sweep_lengths = []
if SWEEP:
    srng = random.Random(1)
    sweep_lengths = sorted(srng.randrange(17, 16380) for _ in range(SWEEP))
    for L in sweep_lengths:
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        rows.append(dict(phase="sweep", prompt_len=L, rep="first", ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e,
                         new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
    # concurrent burst: 32 requests, mixed lengths, 64 output tokens -> prefill + decode mix
    burst = [prompt(srng.randrange(17, 6000)) for _ in range(32)]
    before = entries(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(lambda p: ttft(p, 64), burst))
    rows.append(dict(phase="burst", prompt_len=-1, rep="32 concurrent", ttft_s=max(r[0] for r in res),
                     e2e_s=time.perf_counter() - t0, new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
    print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
end = entries()
summary = dict(rows=rows, entries_at_ready=fam_count(start), new_during_fixed=fam_count(after_fixed - start),
               new_during_serving=fam_count(end - start), new_entries=sorted(end - start),
               sweep_lengths=sweep_lengths)
json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
print("new during serving:", summary["new_during_serving"])
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Both kernels choose a JIT config from the per-rank token count:
- `bf16_mega_gate`: block tokens, MMA CTAs, split-K, expert groups and stages (`heuristics/mega_gate.hpp`). That is 87 configs for per-rank sizes 17 to 8192.
- `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`: `block_m` in {16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 240}.

Startup only compiles the sizes that the profile run and CUDA graph capture hit, here 512 or fewer tokens per rank. Every other prefill size compiles on first use, about 1.7 s per kernel. DeepSeek-V4 needs two gate kernels per size, because hash-routed and bias-routed layers pass different optional inputs.

**Design.** The warmup lives in `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, with the same parts as the existing DeepGEMM warmups:
- A layer predicate that matches DeepSeek-V4's `DeepseekV4MoE` and Kimi K3's `KimiMoE` when they use the native MegaMoE backend.
- A cache constant.
- `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values`: for every per-rank size, it asks DeepGEMM for the `block_m` and, for DeepSeek-V4, the gate config. It keeps the largest size of each distinct config (95 sizes for DeepSeek-V4 here), because DeepSeek-V4 only calls `bf16_mega_gate` above a small token threshold and a config's largest size is always above it. The configs come from DeepGEMM's own getters, so the dedup is exact and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full` would add nothing.
  - Kimi K3 routes with its `GateLinear`, which the bf16x3 router warmup already covers, so for Kimi only `block_m` matters.
  - Kimi's experts call the SiTU variant of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, which picks `block_m` with the same heuristic.
- A private worker and a public loop, an `elif` branch in `_count_warmup_iterations`, and calls in `deep_gemm_warmup`.

The worker runs the whole MoE layer at each size, not the raw kernels:
- The gate gets the same optional inputs it gets in serving.
- Every EP rank runs the same sizes in the same order, which the collective MegaMoE kernel needs.
- It runs under a minimal forward context with a padding mask, because the layer reads `is_padding` from the forward context. This makes the Triton input-staging kernel compile the variants serving uses.
- Under sequence parallelism with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default), ranks above 0 get mask slices at any alignment, so each size runs once with an aligned slice and once with an unaligned one.

The predicate looks the model modules up in `sys.modules`, as other model-specific warmups in this package do (`kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_warmup.py`), so other models import neither model. The cache key reads two DeepSeek-V4-only attributes (`tid2eid`, `image_sentinel_lo`) with `getattr`, because they do not exist on Kimi K3. The two config getters are reached through `_import_deep_gemm`, as in the model code.

`models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` gains one line, which stores `use_sequence_parallel` on `KimiMoE` as `DeepseekV4MoE` already does. The warmup needs it to compute the per-rank token count.

<details>
<summary>Startup trade-off: where the cold warmup time goes</summary>

- About 84% of the cold warmup is serial `nvcc` time for 136 gate kernels (1.7 s each).
- About 14% is about 24 Triton staging variants.
- About 3% is 3 MegaMoE kernels.
- The layer forwards and the size search take under 1 s.

Compiling in parallel threads crashed inside DeepGEMM's JIT, which has no locking and no compile-only API. Parallel compilation would need DeepGEMM changes. vLLM keeps the DeepGEMM cache in `~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm`, so the cold cost is paid once per machine and DeepGEMM version.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining one-time first-request cost</summary>

The first eager prefill whose reduce-scatter falls in the MNNVL multimem size range sets up a symmetric-memory buffer (`_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer`). This adds 60-85 ms to that one request (+61, +66 and +83 ms in three runs). CUDA graph capture skips this setup. It is paid once per server and is not a compile. A torch profile and a request-order test confirm both points.
</details>

**Limitations.** DeepSeek-V4 was validated only on 2x B300 with TP2 + EP2 and Model Runner V2, with and without MTP. Kimi K3 was validated only with a pruned checkpoint on 4x B300, TP4 + EP4, Model Runner V2.
- Not run: Model Runner V1, DP > 1, other EP sizes, EPLB, and routed-experts capture. With EPLB or routed-experts capture on, the warmup forwards would pass dummy tokens to the load recording and the capture hook.

| Code | Result |

| Before | 18 failed, 19 passed |
| After | 37 passed 

### E2E Test
vllm version: 0.31.0(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6)
Model: Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B
Python: 3.12.14
PyTorch: 2.13.0
GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB
CUDA graph: full and piecewise
| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 concurrent requests, mixed ~5s / ~14s unique audios (deterministic crash case) | 8/8 HTTP 500, EngineCore dead | **8/8 OK**, 0 exceptions in logs |
| Single-request multi-clip (unequal clips) — regression check on the 3-D path | OK | **OK** |
| Single clip (batch of one, `unsqueeze` path) — regression check | OK | **OK** |

## Details


### Root Cause
1. The multimodal registry declares `input_audio_features` as `FieldLayout::Batched`, so the Rust frontend emits one item per clip — a 2-D `[n_mels, padded_seq]` tensor, padded to the request's longest clip.
2. The model contract is `MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes(..., dim=1)`: a single flat `[n_mels, total_seq]` tensor.
3. `_reduce_data` stacks only when all shapes are equal; unequal durations (or unequal intra-request padding) → `return batch` raw list.
4. The parser's guard only matches `torch.Tensor` with `dim() == 3`; the list falls through and dies in TensorSchema validation.


## Why this is not a duplicate
Following PR (before 2026.10.10) are related but none of them solved this problem.
- #50958 — canonical model-side fix for familiar bug of Gemma series model. Not involved rust frontend.
- #57146  — It addresses Python preprocessing parity but does not add ragged-list handling or change the Rust preprocessing path.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Reject structural_tag and unhandled specs in backend validation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With the `outlines` or `lm-format-enforcer` structured-output backend, `structural_tag` requests currently pass validation even though neither backend supports them. They then fail in the engine with `ValueError` and finish as `FINISHED_ERROR` instead of being rejected with a 400. This can also affect requests that do not explicitly specify `structural_tag`, since vLLM can construct these constraints internally (e.g. tool parsers using `structural_tag_model` and the Responses API).

This adds a `structural_tag` rejection to both validators, consistent with the existing `grammar` rejections.

Per review, the outlines, lm-format-enforcer and xgrammar validators now also reject any spec they do not handle with a `VLLMValidationError` (400) instead of failing in the engine.

commits.pr_title: [Security] Bound decoded and downloaded media per request
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bound the total downloaded and decoded media in one multimodal request. The same patch was reviewed and approved in the private security fork before public submission.

## Claims

- Enforce one decoded-byte budget across images, audio, and video frames, including direct PIL chat inputs.
- Enforce one streamed HTTP download-byte budget across all media URLs in a request, while retaining the per-response limit.
- Reject requests that exceed either budget and document both configuration controls.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py tests/test_connections.py tests/test_audio_media_size_precheck.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -q` — 44 passed.
- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py -q -k 'request_budget_rejects_second_decoded_audio_clip or video_request_budget_counts_torch_frames'` — 2 passed.
- `/Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run` — passed on all staged files, including Ruff and mypy.
- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py -q -m skip_global_cleanup` — 34 passed, 62 deselected after the audio reservation follow-up.
- `/Users/jperezde/Documents/Dev/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/base.py vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py` — passed, including Ruff and mypy.
- The initial public commit has the same stable patch ID as the approved private commit.

An unrestricted run of those media files on this macOS host segfaulted in `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache` during the global cleanup fixture after the first test. The selected tests above skip that cleanup.

No model evaluation was run. Accepted inputs follow the same decode and serving paths; requests above the new resource limits are rejected by design.

## Details

Previously, a request could pass every per-item media check while still scheduling and retaining many compressed media items before prompt-length admission. The change shares request-scoped budgets across the synchronous and asynchronous chat media paths. HTTP responses are charged as bytes stream in; decoded images are charged before raster allocation, audio decoders reserve capacity before decoding and settle their actual decoded bytes afterward, and video frames are charged during extraction or before JPEG decoding as appropriate. In-flight audio reservations count against the budget for other media. The existing per-item limits remain in effect.

The default decoded budget is 715827880 bytes and the default aggregate HTTP download budget is 256 MB. Operators can configure either limit through the documented environment variables. Requests above a limit now fail rather than consume unbounded frontend resources.

Coverage includes chat completions, messages, and responses that use the Python multimodal tracker; HTTP URLs, `data:` URLs, allowed local files, direct PIL inputs, and video frames. The opt-in Rust frontend and offline user-code helpers are outside this Python parser change.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open and merged upstream PRs for request-wide media budgets, decoded media limits, and HTTP download limits, and inspected the related media PR diffs. The related Rust frontend, audio preprocessing, and Pillow error-handling PRs do not close this Python request-wide path.

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Cursor and OpenAI Codex). The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the diff and validating the change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Don't bake the C128 compressor skip into CUDA graphs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On Model Runner V2, DeepSeek-V4 C128 layers stop writing compressed KV on every step that replays a PIECEWISE CUDA graph. Decode logprobs drift away from prefill, and the gap grows with sequence length. This PR makes the compressor's C128 launch skip apply only when the stream is not capturing.

## Claims

- Fixes C128 compressed-KV writes being dropped on breakable PIECEWISE graph replays (MRV2, the CUDA default).
- No throughput cost: the skip still applies to eager steps, and the compress kernel already gates each token on the GPU.

## Validation

**Regression test:** `tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_c128_skip_is_not_baked_into_cuda_graph`. It captures `DeepseekCompressor.forward` on a batch that completes no 128-token block, then counts kernel launches on replay. On `main` the replay launches nothing; with this PR it launches once. Verified on B300.

**End to end:** vLLM 0.30.0, whose `compressor.py` matches `main` except for two unrelated lines. DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 2x B300, TP2 + EP, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`. 64 prompts, 384 sampled tokens each, base weights. Each server re-scores its own sampled tokens with `prompt_logprobs`. The table reports |decode logprob - prefill logprob| per token:

| Config | mean \|Δ\| | tokens with \|Δ\| > 1 | mean \|Δ\| at tokens 0-127 / 128-383 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enforce_eager` | 0.064 | 0.57% | 0.076 / 0.057 |
| default (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) | 0.118 | 2.14% | 0.089 / 0.133 |
| default + this PR | 0.058 | 0.38% | 0.070 / 0.053 |
| `PIECEWISE` | 0.120 | 2.20% | 0.089 / 0.135 |
| `PIECEWISE` + this PR | 0.059 | 0.40% | 0.071 / 0.053 |

Without the fix, prefill on the same tokens is also nondeterministic run to run: mean k3 0.059 between two scoring passes, against 0.003 with the fix. Prefill chunks that fit a captured size hit the same path.

## Details

`DeepseekCompressor.forward` skips the C128 compress+store when the step's CPU metadata (`c128_boundary`) says no request completes a 128-token block. The old guard excluded only `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`. Since the eager region was narrowed for MRV2, though, the compressor also runs inside breakable PIECEWISE graphs. Capture uses `InputBatch.make_dummy` batches, which never complete a block, so the `return` is recorded into every PIECEWISE graph.

`torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` covers FULL capture too, so it replaces the mode check (the same guard as the indexer short-context shortcut in #52492). MRV1 runs the whole attention prep in the eager region, so it was not affected.

The ROCm two-stage compressor also branches on host `num_decode_tokens` in this region. Both of its launch paths process any token mix, so this PR leaves it alone. Untested on ROCm.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Store conv_kernel - 1 inputs in Mamba2 prefill checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With speculative decoding, the Mamba2 prefill checkpoint (added in #57329) stored conv inputs that were `num_spec` tokens too old. After a prefix-cache restore from that checkpoint, the model read stale conv inputs for its first new tokens and could give a wrong answer. This PR stores only the `conv_kernel_size - 1` inputs that the conv readers use.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs after a prefix-cache hit that restores from a Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoint when MTP or another speculative method is on.
- No change without speculative decoding: then `conv_state.size(-1)` already equals `conv_kernel_size - 1`.
- No change to cache layout, KV capacity or speed.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_store_selects_the_checkpoint_from_all_chunk_states` now runs with `spec_slots` 0 and 3. It checks that the first `state_len` slots hold the newest inputs and that the spec slots stay untouched. All 8 tests in the file pass on GPU with the fix. With the old `store_prefill_checkpoint`, both `spec_slots=3` cases fail and both `spec_slots=0` cases pass.

**End to end.** A Mamba2 hybrid model with one MTP layer, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`, FP8 KV cache, temperature 0, thinking off. These three files are identical at the tested commit and at current `main`.

- **Resend test:** a ~71k-token prompt (a record table; the task copies records 100-160) sent 3 times. Sends 2 and 3 restore 16-31 tokens before the end, on the question.
- **Block-boundary test:** a ~11.6k-token prompt whose key digits sit right before a 4,544-token (4,416 with 5 draft tokens) block boundary, so the restore lands at that boundary.
- **Wrong** = a copied record differs from the source table.

| Setup | Test | Wrong before | Wrong after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 draft tokens | resend, 24 resends | 8 / 24 | 0 / 24 |
| 7 draft tokens, default `--prefix-match-unit` | block boundary, 12 resends | 10 / 12 | 0 / 12 |
| 5 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting | resend, 24 resends | 6 / 24 | 0 / 24 |
| 5 draft tokens, default `--prefix-match-unit` | block boundary, 12 resends | 12 / 12 | 0 / 12 |
| P/D disaggregated (NIXL), 7 draft tokens | resend, 24 resends | 13 / 24 | 0 / 24 |

- First sends (no cache hit) were wrong 0 times before and after, and gave the same text before and after.
- All 270 sends restored at the predicted token count, so the tests went through the restore path.
- Controls before the fix: prefix caching off gave 0 / 24 wrong; speculative decoding off gave 0 / 24 wrong.
- KV cache size and resend latency did not change.

## Details

**Root cause.** With speculative decoding the paged conv state has `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` slots (`mamba_utils.py`). `store_prefill_checkpoint` set `state_len = conv_state.size(-1)` and wrote inputs `[ckpt - state_len, ckpt)` into slots `0..state_len-1`, oldest first. Every reader takes slots `0..conv_kernel_size-2` as the newest inputs:

- `causal_conv1d_fn` uses `state_len = KERNEL_WIDTH - 1`.
- `causal_conv1d_update` reads from slot `num_accepted_tokens - 1`, which is 0 for a restored request.

So slots `0..2` (conv kernel 4) held inputs that were `num_spec` tokens too old. `--prefix-match-unit 16` makes such restores frequent: the restore point lands 16-31 tokens before the prompt end. The default unit restores at block boundaries, which the same export also writes.

**Fix.** `store_prefill_checkpoint` takes a required keyword `state_len`, and its only caller passes `self.conv_kernel_size - 1`. `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` already takes an explicit `state_len` for the same reason. The kernel keeps the physical strides, so both conv layouts (dim-first and the transposed view) work. The spec slots of the checkpoint block are not written. Nothing reads them before the next update rewrites all slots, and before this change they held no useful data either.

**Other paths checked.** The align-mode copies, the shared-prefix checkpoint, NIXL transfer and CPU offload copy whole conv rows or already use `conv_kernel_size - 1`. They need no change.

**Limitation.** This covers Mamba2 only. When `state_len` is unset, `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` still falls back to the full conv width.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The NVIDIA V1 Attention steps (H100 and B200) were split into 2 fixed pytest shards (`--shard-id` / `--num-shards`, `parallelism: 2`), and each shard still takes 46–51 min. This turns each into one plain `pytest -v -s v1/attention` step with `automatic_shard: true`, the same as #60492, #60662, #60757 and #60858.

The pipeline generator then plans the shards at bootstrap from main's per-file timings. It splits the two big MLA files by test function. Planned shards on current timings:

| `v1-attention-b200` | 6 | 16.4 ×5, 19.1 |

The AMD mirrors (MI300, MI355 DPX) are unchanged. They keep their fixed pytest shards, because `automatic_shard` covers NVIDIA steps only, so the shard args and `parallelism: 2` move into the mirror config.

## Test Plan

[Buildkite build 94185](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94185) ran only these two steps. Every shard passed, and the shard plugin was active in all of them. The baseline is main build 94136, whose two fixed shards are summed.

| B200 | 6: 15.4, 16.3, 15.6, 10.2, 9.3, 19.4 | 46.2–52.2 → **19.4** | 100–104 → 86 | 3539 = 3539 |

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Tune Triton GDN decode tiles on SM100-family GPUs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Tune the existing Triton packed GDN decode launch on SM100-family GPUs. Smaller value tiles improve utilization at small batches and reduce per-CTA work with FP32 recurrent state.

## Claims

- **1.34–1.74× faster kernel** at B=1–64 for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP4 layout with FP32 state on GB300; **1.21–1.34×** at B=1/2/4 with BF16 state.
- **1.0–2.2% higher output throughput** in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 serving, with unchanged full GSM8K and C=8 check scores.
- A 12-line dispatch change; existing kernel math and interfaces are preserved. FlashInfer is benchmarked as a comparison candidate only and is **not integrated by this PR**.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

GB300 (152 SMs), BF16 QKV, `(H, HV)=(4, 12)`, `K=V=128`, Q/K normalization enabled. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. CUPTI kernel time with CUDA graphs and cold L2; medians of seven shuffled rounds, 40 samples per call. Main uses BV32; PR uses the tile selected by the heuristic.

**FlashInfer is an ideal-input comparison:** `gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(backend="flashinfer")` with contiguous Q/K/V prepared outside the timed call. These numbers exclude layout-conversion/copy costs and do not represent an integrated vLLM serving path. The E2E results below compare main against tuned Triton only.

**FP32 recurrent state**

| Batch | Main (µs) | PR (µs) | Speedup | FlashInfer, not integrated (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.36 | 3.09 | 1.74× | 4.22 |
| 2 | 5.60 | 3.30 | 1.70× | 4.43 |
| 4 | 6.08 | 3.78 | 1.61× | 4.93 |
| 8 | 7.14 | 5.09 | 1.40× | 5.73 |
| 16 | 8.99 | 6.56 | 1.37× | 7.18 |
| 32 | 15.65 | 11.07 | 1.41× | 11.78 |
| 64 | 24.21 | 18.06 | 1.34× | 19.54 |

**BF16 recurrent state**

| Batch | Main (µs) | PR (µs) | Speedup | FlashInfer, not integrated (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.00 | 3.10 | 1.29× | 3.36 |
| 2 | 4.19 | 3.12 | 1.34× | 3.36 |
| 4 | 4.38 | 3.62 | 1.21× | 3.71 |
| 8 | 4.85 | 4.85 | 1.00× | 4.11 |
| 16 | 6.05 | 6.05 | 1.00× | 6.08 |
| 32 | 8.19 | 8.19 | 1.00× | 9.09 |
| 64 | 14.14 | 14.14 | 1.00× | 12.72 |

For BF16 state at B≥8, the PR selects unchanged BV32; the main and PR columns therefore use the same measured launch.

Triton output and recurrent state matched the baseline bit-for-bit in these checks. FlashInfer is not bit-identical: output checks used `atol=rtol=1e-3`; FP32-state checks used `atol=rtol=1e-5`, while BF16-state checks required `atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2` after ten recurrent updates. No FlashInfer model-accuracy claim is made.

<details>
<summary>TP generalization</summary>

GB300, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next local head layouts `(H, HV)`, BF16 activations and FP32 state. Speedup is main / PR kernel time; median of five shuffled rounds with 40 CUPTI samples each. Eager execution and ten recurrent CUDA-graph updates matched bit-for-bit.

| Batch | TP1 (16, 48) | TP2 (8, 24) | TP4 (4, 12) | TP8 (2, 6) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.56× | 1.69× | 1.80× | 1.87× |
| 2 | 1.40× | 1.57× | 1.74× | 1.77× |
| 4 | 1.38× | 1.36× | 1.62× | 1.75× |
| 8 | 1.41× | 1.41× | 1.37× | 1.63× |
| 16 | 1.33× | 1.40× | 1.39× | 1.47× |
| 32 | 1.19× | 1.30× | 1.40× | 1.36× |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark reproduction</summary>

Run from the feature checkout in an installed CUDA development venv with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and `cupti-python`. The script loads the baseline kernel from upstream commit `28d679e762`, uses the checkout's PR dispatch, and prepares the FlashInfer inputs before timing. Save as `bench_gdn.py` and run `.venv/bin/python bench_gdn.py`.

```python
import importlib.util
import json
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from flashinfer.gdn_decode import gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.fused_recurrent import (
    fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode as tuned,
)

BASE = '28d679e762a0b6ed560d767a76ebe02699bf5c46'
FILE = 'vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py'
source = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'{BASE}:{FILE}'], text=True)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / 'baseline.py'
    path.write_text(source)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        'vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops._gdn_baseline', path
    )
    baseline = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(baseline)

    generator = torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(1234)
    order_rng = random.Random(1234)
    for state_dtype in [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]:
        for batch in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]:
            mixed = torch.randn(batch, 2560, device='cuda',
                                dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator) * .1
            a = torch.randn(batch, 12, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                            generator=generator)
            b = torch.randn(batch, 12, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                            generator=generator)
            al = torch.zeros(12, device='cuda')
            dt = torch.zeros_like(al)
            ids = torch.arange(1, batch + 1, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
            initial = torch.randn(batch + 1, 12, 128, 128, device='cuda',
                                  dtype=state_dtype, generator=generator) * .1
            # FlashInfer ideal case: Q/K/V layout conversion is outside timing.
            q = mixed[:, :512].view(batch, 1, 4, 128).contiguous()
            k = mixed[:, 512:1024].view(batch, 1, 4, 128).contiguous()
            v = mixed[:, 1024:].view(batch, 1, 12, 128).contiguous()
            states = {name: initial.clone() for name in ['main', 'PR', 'FI']}
            outputs = {name: torch.empty(batch, 1, 12, 128, device='cuda',
                                        dtype=torch.bfloat16) for name in states}
            calls = {}
            for name, fn in [('main', baseline.fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode),
                             ('PR', tuned)]:
                calls[name] = lambda fn=fn, name=name: fn(
                    mixed, a, b, al, dt, 128**-.5, states[name], outputs[name], ids, True
                )
            calls['FI'] = lambda: gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(
                q=q, k=k, v=v, state=None, A_log=al, a=a.view(batch, 1, 12),
                dt_bias=dt, b=b.view(batch, 1, 12), scale=128**-.5,
                output=outputs['FI'], use_qk_l2norm=True,
                initial_state=states['FI'], initial_state_indices=ids,
                backend='flashinfer',
            )
            for call in calls.values():
                for _ in range(10):
                    call()
            torch.testing.assert_close(outputs['PR'], outputs['main'], atol=0, rtol=0)
            torch.testing.assert_close(states['PR'], states['main'], atol=0, rtol=0)
            torch.testing.assert_close(outputs['FI'], outputs['main'], atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
            tol = (1e-5, 1e-5) if state_dtype == torch.float32 else (1e-3, 1e-2)
            torch.testing.assert_close(states['FI'], states['main'], atol=tol[0], rtol=tol[1])
            times = {name: [] for name in calls}
            for _ in range(7):
                order = list(calls)
                order_rng.shuffle(order)
                for name in order:
                    states[name].copy_(initial)
                    for _ in range(30):
                        calls[name]()
                    times[name].append(statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
                        calls[name], dry_run_iters=5, repeat_iters=40,
                        use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                    )) * 1000)
            print(json.dumps(dict(batch=batch, state=str(state_dtype),
                                  us={name: statistics.median(t) for name, t in times.items()})))
```

</details>

### E2E performance

 Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, revision `236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13`; four GB300s on the same node, TP4 with expert parallelism, MRv2, no speculative decoding, prefix caching disabled, NUMA binding enabled, FP8 main KV and FP8 indexer caches. Model activations are BF16; the checkpoint's default recurrent state is FP32. Both arms use FlashInfer autotuning, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, and `max_num_seqs=256`.

Real NVIDIA SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` prompts, dataset revision `454f88454792dfa3ccfd7ef15fff248efde44cd1`, capped at 8192 raw prompt tokens; 1024 output tokens with `ignore_eos`. Closed-loop concurrency sweep, five warmup requests per point, `max(32, 10 × concurrency)` measured requests, fixed seed 0. One serial sweep per arm. Output tokens/s covers the full benchmark window.

| Concurrency | Baseline output tok/s | Tuned output tok/s | Change | Baseline TTFT P50/P95 (ms) | Tuned TTFT P50/P95 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 246.1 | 249.5 | +1.4% | 173.1 / 180.2 | 172.6 / 178.6 |
| 2 | 416.7 | 424.9 | +2.0% | 250.5 / 329.4 | 249.3 / 331.4 |
| 4 | 714.7 | 730.4 | +2.2% | 477.5 / 670.1 | 474.4 / 492.1 |
| 8 | 1200.1 | 1217.8 | +1.5% | 586.6 / 878.3 | 586.6 / 876.0 |
| 16 | 1943.3 | 1967.9 | +1.3% | 993.7 / 1651.9 | 985.3 / 1646.6 |
| 32 | 2868.2 | 2895.8 | +1.0% | 1787.7 / 3196.3 | 1795.0 / 3200.3 |
| 64 | 3970.6 | 4014.4 | +1.1% | 3395.5 / 6092.3 | 3361.7 / 6029.8 |

All 1304 measured requests per arm succeeded and produced exactly 1024 output tokens.

### Accuracy

 GSM8K, five-shot chat completions, thinking disabled, temperature 0, maximum 2048 output tokens:

| Configuration | Questions | Baseline flexible / strict | Tuned flexible / strict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C=1, full test set | 1319 | 97.04% / 97.12% | 97.04% / 97.12% |
| C=8, concurrency check | 64 | 98.44% / 98.44% | 98.44% / 98.44% |

No per-question scores changed. Both arms had zero request errors, null answers, or empty responses. The same two questions hit the output cap in the full run; neither arm truncated at C=8. Generated text was not bit-identical for every question: three responses differed at C=1 and twenty at C=8, without changing their scores.

### Tests

- Focused GPU reference suite: **14 passed on GB300**, covering BV4/BV8/BV32, independent activation/state dtypes, contiguous/strided QKV, and padded/null state slots. Reproduce with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py -q`.
- Wrapper validation: **136 FP16/BF16-activation cases** using this dispatch matched output and updated state bit-for-bit. Broader sweeps covered Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 head layouts, TP settings, uneven batches, and normalization on/off on GB200 and GB300. 148-SM green contexts covered the occupancy boundary relevant to B200; this is not a physical B200 performance measurement.
- Natural MRv2 graph capture exercised BV4 and BV8 on all four ranks. The existing B200 CI job `kernels-fla-ops-test-b200` runs the updated reference suite.
- Post-rebase changed-file pre-commit passed, including ruff, mypy, and test tethering; `git diff --check` passed.

<summary>Serving, accuracy, and lint reproduction</summary>

Post-rebase checks:

```bash
git diff upstream/main --check
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py \
  tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py
# Passed, including ruff, mypy, and Buildkite test tethering.
```

Serving command for each arm, using its own matching runtime:

```bash

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=0 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \

  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1
```

The performance client was `vllm-bench 0.1.0`. Export the pinned SPEED-Bench parquet rows to a JSON array retaining the `turns` field, then run this per concurrency point:

```bash
# C: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; N: max(32, 10*C).
# TOKENIZER: the snapshot path for the pinned model revision.
vllm-bench --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tokenizer "$TOKENIZER" \
  --dataset-name speed-bench --dataset-path speed-bench.json \
  --speed-bench-config throughput_8k --speed-bench-max-input-len 8192 \
  --output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 5 \
  --max-concurrency "$C" --num-prompts "$N" --seed 0 --no-oversample \
  --extra-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false},"temperature":0}' \
  --percentile-metrics ttft --metric-percentiles 50,95 \

```

```bash

  --api-type chat_completions --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --think false \
  --extra-params '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}' \
  --shot-num 5 --epoch-num 1 --concurrency "$C" \
  --save-interactions --output-dir accuracy
```

</details>

## Details

For `K=V=128` on CUDA SM100-family GPUs, select BV4 when `B × HV <= 64`, BV8 otherwise for FP32 recurrent state, and retain BV32 otherwise. Warps and stages stay at 1 and 3. The baseline launches `4 × B × HV` CTAs; BV4 provides eight times as many at small batches. Larger batches with 16-bit state keep BV32 because smaller tiles regressed those workloads in tuning.

The capability query uses the input tensor's device. Existing MRv2 warmup/graph capture compiles the reachable variants; no extra warmup, GPU synchronization, or online autotuning is introduced. Prefill and speculative verification use separate paths.

The serving A/B used baseline `28d679e762` and the PR's GDN module in fresh processes on the same node, with identical diagnostics. GPU validation was collected before rebasing onto `e2ad0ce5f5`; all three patches and the changed GDN source/test files are unchanged. Post-rebase lint passed; no further serving sweep was run.

Duplicate checks found no open PR implementing this SM100-family policy. Related [#54181](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54181) tunes SM120, [#60400](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60400) tunes ROCm, and [#60403](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60403) adds opt-in FlashInfer decode; their hardware/backend scope differs.
