commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fall back to auto for unquantized MoE layers when --moe-backend is marlin
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #56832. With `--moe-backend marlin`, an unquantized MoE layer (here, the BF16 MTP draft of an NVFP4 model) now uses the auto-selected unquantized backend instead of raising `ValueError`. `humming` already works this way. Related: #56964 discusses the same fix.

## Claims

- `vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --moe-backend marlin --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` now starts and serves requests with MTP speculative decoding. Before this change, loading the draft model failed with `ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE`.
- Quantized MoE layers still use Marlin. Only unquantized MoE layers change: they now use the auto-selected backend instead of raising.
- A new unit test checks that `marlin` and `humming` give the same unquantized backend as `auto`.

## Validation

Hardware: 2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2. Base commit `92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` (`0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`).

Reproducer (the command from the issue):

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
```

To check that the draft model really runs, send one request after startup and read the spec-decode counters:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 * 23? Answer briefly."}],"max_tokens":400,"temperature":0}'
curl -s http://localhost:8000/metrics | grep -E "^vllm:spec_decode_num_(drafts|draft_tokens|accepted_tokens)_total"
```

| Tree | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| base | 2 (one in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a…` image, one in an editable install) | 2 of 2 failed. Both TP workers raised `ValueError` while building the MTP draft's MoE layer, about 2.5 minutes after start. No requests served. | | base + this PR | 2 (editable install) | 2 of 2 started and served the request. The answers were correct (391, and 408 in the second run, which asked for 12 × 34). Draft acceptance was 73.3% (33/45 tokens) and 76.9% (30/39 tokens). No `Traceback` in either log. |

Before:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE. Expected one of ['triton', 'batched_triton', 'flashinfer_trtllm', 'flashinfer_cutlass', 'aiter'].
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (log excerpt):

```
[nvfp4.py:268] Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'VLLM_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN', 'HUMMING', 'EMULATION'].
[unquantized.py:365] Using FlashInfer CUTLASS Unquantized MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FlashInfer TRTLLM', 'FlashInfer CUTLASS', 'TRITON', 'BATCHED_TRITON'].
INFO:     Application startup complete.
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 3.20, ... Accepted: 33 tokens, Drafted: 45 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.800, 0.800, 0.600, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 73.3%
```

Unit test (run with `--noconftest` because `tblib`, which the top-level conftest imports, was not installed in the test environment):

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest
27 passed, 3 skipped
```

With the old condition put back, the new `marlin` case fails with the error from the issue and the `humming` case passes. The file already runs in CI through `pytest -v -s kernels/moe` (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`). The end-to-end check above was run by hand, outside CI. `pre-commit` passes on both changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `--moe-backend` is one global value (`KernelConfig.moe_backend`). It reaches every MoE layer, quantized or not. The MTP draft inherits it unless `speculative_config.moe_backend` is set. This checkpoint has NVFP4 main experts, but it excludes `mtp.*` from quantization and stores those experts in BF16. So `mtp.layers.48.mlp.experts` correctly gets `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, with `moe_backend='marlin'`. A debug run showed that the draft keeps `ModelOptNvFp4Config` and gets no quant method only because its prefix matches `mtp.*`, so the draft is not losing its quant config by mistake. Marlin has no BF16 MoE kernel: `MarlinExperts._supports_quant_scheme` lists only quantized schemes. `select_unquantized_moe_backend` already lets `humming`, another quantization-only backend, fall through to `auto` (#41652), but `marlin` was not in that list. So it reached `map_unquantized_backend`, which has no entry for it and raises.

**Fix.** Add `"marlin"` to the fall-through list in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/unquantized.py`, and update the comment. Quantized layers go through other oracles, so they keep Marlin. The NVFP4 experts above still log `Using 'MARLIN'`.

**Why the draft override is not enough.** Users can work around the draft case with `"moe_backend": "auto"` in `--speculative-config`, but that override only reaches the draft. In a quantized checkpoint, MoE layers of the main model that are left unquantized (`modules_to_not_convert` / `ignore` / `exclude_modules`) go through the same function with the same global value. No flag reaches them. This change covers them too, but that case was not run end to end here.

**Behavior change.** `--moe-backend marlin` on a model whose MoE layers are all unquantized used to fail at load with a clear error. Now it loads on the auto-selected backend. Only the `Using ... Unquantized MoE backend` info line shows that Marlin was not used. This matches `humming`. No existing test asserts the old error: the tests that set `marlin` all use quantized models, which go through a different oracle.

**Limitations.** Other quantization-only backends still raise the same error for unquantized layers, for example `flashinfer_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_b12x`, `b12x`, `cutlass` and `deep_gemm`. This PR leaves them alone to keep the fix small. A general rule ("no unquantized kernel → auto") could replace the list if maintainers prefer. For the same reason, the comment in `vllm/config/speculative.py` about the draft inheriting the target's `--moe-backend` is still true for those backends, so it is unchanged.

---

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Fuse MoE routers that score after the top-k
commits.pr_body:
Three related changes to the Transformers modeling backend's MoE path, smallest
to largest in blast radius.

## 1. `MoEBlockFuser._match_router` accepts scoring on either side of the top-k

`_match_router` only looked for `softmax`/`sigmoid` *upstream* of the routing
top-k. A family of HF routers scores the selection instead:

```python
# GraniteMoeTopKRouter, AriaTextTopKRouter, JetMoE, ...
top_k_logits, top_k_index = router_logits.topk(self.top_k, dim=-1)
top_k_weights = torch.softmax(top_k_logits, dim=-1)
```

These did not match, so the whole block fell back to routing in Transformers and
smuggling `topk_ids` through a custom op. They now fuse.

The two placements are equivalent: `sigmoid` is elementwise, so scoring before or
after the selection is identical; a `softmax` over the selected logits equals a
softmax over every logit with the selected weights renormalized, since the
full-vocabulary denominator cancels.

## 2. `renormalize` is read from the router's graph, not guessed from the config

vLLM's kernel always scores all `E` experts and then selects, so its weights sum
to less than 1. Reproducing a router that softmaxes the selection alone requires
`renormalize=True`. The previous logic was `norm_topk_prob` if present, else
`top_k > 1`, which is wrong for a router that uses raw softmax-over-all weights
(`RoutingMethodType.Default`) and for `top_k=1`, where renormalizing forces the
single gate to exactly 1.0.

`_match_router` now reports what the router actually does:

- `True` if it softmaxes the selection, or divides the top-k weights by their sum
  (the walk goes through the denominator's input cone, so it absorbs the
  `+ 1e-20` spelling that 17 models in Transformers use).
- `False` if a complete trace shows it does neither.
- `None` only if tracing stopped before it could tell, in which case the previous
  config logic still applies.

This is more reliable than reading the config, not less: `norm_topk_prob` is a
Python bool that fx resolves at trace time, so the graph already reflects it.
`Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` traces to 13 nodes with `sum`/`truediv` when the flag is on
and 11 without. It also handles per-layer heterogeneity for free, since `match()`
runs per block against that block's own router instance rather than indexing a
config list by `extract_layer_index`.

## 3. `_infer_meta` no longer recurses until the stack runs out

While tracing, fx patches `nn.Module.__getattr__` to record `get_attr` nodes.
`_infer_meta`'s `get_attr` branch read the parameter's value through that patched
hook, so inferring the meta value of a `get_attr` created another `get_attr`,
which inferred its meta value, and so on until `RecursionError` — swallowed by the
`contextlib.suppress(Exception)` in `create_proxy`, leaving a complete but
massively duplicated graph.

This fires for any module reading an `nn.Parameter` directly in `forward`, which
is every HF v5 `TopKRouter` and every `RMSNorm`. Nodes in the returned graph,
before and after:

| module | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DeepseekV3TopkRouter` | 5519 | 31 |
| `GraniteMoeTopKRouter` | 1970 | 10 |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` | 1775 | 11 |
| `Qwen3MoeRMSNorm` | 600 | 12 |
| `Qwen3MoeMLP` (only `nn.Linear` children) | 7 | 7 |

How many repeats got recorded depended on how much stack was left, so repeated
traces of the same module disagreed with each other. Matching that only walked
`all_input_nodes` upstream survived this; anything reading `users` did not, which
is what made change 1 necessary to fix first.

Meta execution now runs under `_unpatched_modules()`, restoring both `__call__`
(which the `call_module` branch already did) and `__getattr__`.

## Testing

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers -q
111 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 15.38s

$ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fx_utils.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/moe.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py \
    tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py
(all hooks passed)
```

New cases in `tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py`: post-top-k scoring
for both `softmax` and `sigmoid`, and `renormalize` resolving to `True` for
divide-by-sum, `True` for an epsilon-offset denominator, `False` for a router that
scales its weights instead, and `None` for a router whose trace is cut short.

Spot-checked against the real Transformers routers on the meta device:

| router | `_match_router` |
| --- | --- |
| `GraniteMoeTopKRouter` | `('softmax', float32, True)` |
| `AriaTextTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, True)` |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` (`norm_topk_prob=True`) | `('softmax', None, True)` |
| `Qwen3MoeTopKRouter` (`norm_topk_prob=False`) | `('softmax', None, False)` |
| `DeepseekV3TopkRouter` | `('sigmoid', float32, True)` |
| `DeepseekV2TopkRouter` | `('softmax', float32, False)` |
| `OlmoeTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, False)` |
| `FlexOlmoTopKRouter` | `('softmax', None, False)` |

These agree with vLLM's native implementations, which hardcode the same values:
`granitemoe.py:106` `renormalize=True`, `olmoe.py:100` `renormalize=False`,
`deepseek_v2.py:381` `renormalize=config.norm_topk_prob`.

## Model evaluation

**Not run.** This change affects model output and I do not have a GPU available,
so I could not run `tests/evals/gsm8k` or `vllm bench`. Flagging it explicitly
rather than leaving it for a reviewer to ask.

The two things most worth a real model behind them:

- GraniteMoE and Aria now take the fused path instead of routing in Transformers.
- Change 3 is shared by every fuser, not just MoE, so GLU/QKV/RMSNorm/MLA/Attention
  matching across the whole Transformers backend now runs against different (and
  correct) graphs.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches `transformers/fusers/moe.py`, `transformers/fx_utils.py`,
`MoEBlockFuser` or `_match_router` (`gh pr list --search` on each). The nearest
neighbours are #53811 (removes native LongCat) and #55690 (QKV-Fuser for Gemma4),
neither of which overlaps.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I have reviewed every
changed line and ran the tests quoted above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Run the AITER AR+RMSNorm fallback test on the platform…
commits.pr_body:
`tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py::test_rocm_aiter_gemma_rmsnorm_falls_back_after_allreduce` fails in `:amd: (MI355) Distributed Features`. The test was added yesterday by #58547, together with the fallback it covers.

[The failing job.](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94315/list?jid=01a131ef-a206-418e-b06e-7a6311a6c957&tab=output)

> NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm_aiter::fused_add_rms_norm' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend. This could be because the operator doesn't exist for this backend, or was omitted during the selective/custom build process. 'vllm_aiter::fused_add_rms_norm' is only available for these backends: [CUDA, Meta, BackendSelect, ...].

The test builds its tensors on the CPU, while the fallback it exercises leaves Python through `torch.ops.vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm`. That op is registered for the platform's dispatch key alone, which is `CUDA` on a ROCm build, so a CPU tensor has nothing to dispatch to and the test fails before reaching any of its assertions. The two neighbouring tests in `test_quick_all_reduce.py` do pass with CPU tensors, because their path calls into AITER directly with no registered op in between.

Building the tensors on `current_platform.device_type` is enough, which is what 125 other test files already do. The AITER kernel behind the op stays faked, so the test needs neither real hardware nor an AITER install, and it still passes on a CPU only box, where that device and the dispatch key are both CPU. No `skipif` is needed and nothing outside the test changes.

Worth noting that this is not AMD specific. `vllm/kernels/__init__.py` imports the AITER ops unconditionally and the registration does not need AITER installed, so the op exists on NVIDIA builds too and the test would fail there in exactly the same way. It is only ever run in the AMD step, so nobody sees it.

## Test Result

The test passes on MI355, and the two neighbouring tests in `test_quick_all_reduce.py` still pass.

commits.pr_title: [Tests][Mamba] Wait for accepted counts in fake MTP proposer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1` / `_mrv1_async`, failing on `main` since #61134 on H200 MIG and MI250 (e.g. [main build #94362](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94362#01a1333b-d247-49be-b767-84df48ec72c7)): `ValueError: Mamba state is not equal for key: 576 at index 0`. Test-only change.

## Claims

- The test's fake MTP proposer read `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` before the same-step non-blocking D2H copy finished, so a GPU lagging behind the host fed off-by-one draft tokens. It now waits on `num_accepted_tokens_event` first.
- No runner change: the real proposer uses GPU tensors, and the runner already synchronizes that event in `_prepare_inputs` before reading the CPU counts.

## Validation

The failure does not reproduce on GB200 as-is (fast GPU hides the race), so I injected GPU lag with a `sitecustomize.py` that runs `torch.cuda._sleep(20_000_000)` (~10 ms) at the start of every `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`:

| GB200, `-k test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1*` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no injected lag | pass | pass |
| injected GPU lag, sync | **fail** (`key: 576 at index 0`, same as CI) | pass |
| injected GPU lag, async | — | pass |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py -k "test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv1" -s
```

`pre-commit` passes.

## Details

- In `accept_2_1`, the mismatching conv state at token 576 differed only in row 0 (the token carried over from the previous step); rows 1-2, computed in the current step, matched the reference bit-exactly. That row was produced from a wrong draft token: the fake proposer computed its offset from a stale `num_accepted_tokens_cpu` (still the value written before `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu`'s non-blocking D2H landed).
- Why now: before #61134, FP8 dummy weights were ±1e-3 (mostly rounded to 0 in E4M3), so conv states were ~0 regardless of the input token and the comparison passed vacuously. With ±1 FP8 dummy weights the states are meaningful, and slow CI GPUs (16-SM H200 MIG slice, MI250) expose the race. `main` passed this test at c6566bb9f6 and fails from the next build onward; the other commits in that window only touch DSv4.1/ROCm or Intel CI yaml.
- Related but distinct: #51571 (row-ownership race of the same CPU tensor under async scheduling, fixed in the runner by #51599/#53919). This PR touches neither; the test runs a single request and fails without async scheduling too.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Don't create hash directories on cache-miss lookups in ECExampleConnector
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`ECExampleConnector.has_cache_item()` resolves the safetensors path via
`_generate_filename_debug()`, which auto-creates the `<mm_hash>/` directory.
Since `has_cache_item()` is called from the scheduler's encoder-input
admission check and from `update_state_after_alloc()` on every multimodal
allocation, **every probed-but-missed hash leaves an empty directory in
shared storage**. On a long-lived deployment the EC storage root accumulates
one empty directory per unique missed hash, making the cache impossible to
inspect and polluting any listing-based tooling/backup jobs.

Fixes #60820

## Approach

Keep auto-creation on the **save** path (where the directory is actually
needed) and disable it on the **lookup** path:

- `_found_match_for_mm_data()` now passes `create_folder=False` to
  `_generate_filename_debug()`.
- `_generate_filename_debug()` gains a `create_folder: bool = True`
  parameter, forwarded to `_generate_foldername_debug()`. Defaults are
  unchanged, so `save_caches()` / `start_load_caches()` behavior is
  identical.

No behavioral change beyond the filesystem side effect.

## Testing

- Added `test_has_cache_item_miss_creates_no_folder` to the existing
  `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_ec_example_connector.py`: a cache-miss
  lookup leaves no empty folder in shared storage.
- Also verified on a live A100 EPD testbed against a producer-role
  connector: `VERIFY-OK`.

## Notes

- Observed on a live deployment; the same code paths exist on current main.
- `start_load_caches` is untouched: it only loads hashes that
  `has_cache_item()` has already confirmed to exist.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Mamba] Remove leftovers of mamba_cache_mode="all"
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #58997. Removes what was left of `mamba_cache_mode="all"` and deprecates `--mamba-cache-mode`, which no longer has any effect.

## Changes

- **KV cache manager:** `MambaManager` asserts that prefix caching runs only with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. A `"none"` group under a caching manager used to silently run all-mode dense caching. Production never pairs them: `MambaModelConfig` ties `"align"` to prefix caching on and `"none"` to off.
- **CLI:** deprecated `--mamba-cache-mode`. `MambaModelConfig` already overwrote any user value (`"align"` iff prefix caching is on), so the flag is now ignored with a warning and will be removed in v0.33.0. ReplaySSM/RecoverSSM errors, config docstrings, docs, CI configs and e2e tests now refer to prefix caching instead of the flag.
- **Kernels:** dropped the APC per-block state inputs from Triton `causal_conv1d_fn` / `causal_conv1d_update`. No caller used them, and the non-APC path is unchanged. XPU is untouched.
  - Two all-mode leftovers are kept on purpose:
    - SSD's `return_intermediate_states`: #57329 uses it for Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints.
    - CUDA `selective_scan_fwd`'s per-block state outputs: Mamba1 internal checkpoints will need mid-prefill state output from that kernel.
  - Conv-window checkpoints do not need the `causal_conv1d` inputs, because they are written from the pre-conv input.
- **Models:** removed the `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` flag. Its only reader was the all → align fallback deleted in #58997. Dropped the `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching` base from hybrid models, since `IsHybrid` already declares `get_mamba_state_copy_func(s)`. Only attention-free `Mamba`/`Mamba2` keep it.
- **Docs/comments:** fixed stale all-mode descriptions.
- **Tests:**
  - Mamba prefix-caching tests use `"align"`. `req0` is split so align keeps a state at the shared prefix.
  - Dropped `test_mamba_shared_prefix_survives_zero_retention`. Its flow is covered by `test_mamba_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention`.
  - The simple-offload DCP geometry test uses a replicated attention group.
  - `test_p_side_chunked_prefill_mamba` runs without prefix caching.
  - Fixed `test_mixer2_gated_norm_multi_gpu`, which also failed on `main`: its spawned workers had no vLLM config.

## Compatibility

- `ModelConfig.supports_mamba_prefix_caching` is removed. A leftover `supports_mamba_prefix_caching` class attribute is ignored.
- `--mamba-cache-mode` / `EngineArgs.mamba_cache_mode` is deprecated: ignored with a warning, removed in v0.33.0. Behavior is unchanged for Mamba models, since the value was already overwritten. `CacheConfig.mamba_cache_mode` stays and is still derived from `enable_prefix_caching`.

## Validation

GB200:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py   # 560 passed, 2 skipped
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k mamba     # 18 passed
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/test_config.py   # 546 passed, 5 skipped
```

`EngineArgs(model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", ...).create_engine_config()`: no flag → `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="none"` with prefix caching → deprecation warning, `align`; `mamba_cache_mode="align"` without prefix caching → `none`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR covers these #58997 leftovers.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Qwen4Exp] FP8 QSA main KV cache on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86)
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` crashes for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Ampere (sm_80, sm_86): the QSA Triton kernels use an `fp8e4nv` pointer, which Triton supports only from sm_89. Below sm_89 this PR reads the e4m3 cache as bytes and decodes it exactly with a bit cast. Same flag and cache format; BF16 and sm_89+ do not change.

**Why Ampere:** vLLM already enables an FP8 KV cache on sm_80 for other backends (FlashInfer, #24577); this model's QSA path is the gap. We serve Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 8× A100, where FP8 doubles the KV capacity, and @nkuhn-vmw runs it on 4× RTX 3090 (sm_86).

## Results (8× A100-40GB, TP8 + EP)

- Fixes the crash: 4 FP8 attention tests that fail on `main` at sm_80 now pass.
- KV cache capacity ×1.83 (1.16M → 2.13M tokens). sm_86 (4× RTX 3090, by @nkuhn-vmw): ×1.87, GSM8K unchanged.
- Attention kernel time, FP8 vs BF16 cache: 0.92–1.14×. End to end at concurrency 8, client TPOT p50 is 6 % higher with FP8 (see "Decode cost").
- Prompt-logprob difference FP8 vs BF16 is close to BF16 run-to-run noise (σ 0.115 vs 0.111 nats, 150k tokens).
- Serving the full MLPerf agentic dataset (multi-turn coding, prompts up to ~200k tokens), 3 runs per row:

| Concurrency | KV cache | Requests/s | TTFT p95 (s) | Prefix-cache hit | Prompt tokens received / computed in prefill, per run (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | BF16 | 1.15–1.24 | 1.1–1.3 | 97–98 % | 301–319 / 5.0–7.8 |
| 8 | FP8 | 1.20–1.23 | 1.2 | 98.5 % | 322–326 / 4.7–4.9 |
| 12 | BF16 | 0.96–1.09 | 18–27 | 90–92 % | 235–277 / 21–23 |
| 12 | FP8 | **1.59** | **1.5** | 98.5 % | **457–462 / 6.8–7.1** |
| 16 | BF16 | 0.58–0.64 | 73–83 | 73–77 % | 126–143 / 32–33 |
| 16 | FP8 | **1.58–1.63** | **7.5–10.4** | 96–97 % | **426–445 / 14–15** |

At concurrency 16, FP8 serves 2.7× the requests with ~9× lower p95 TTFT: it receives 3.4× more prompt tokens but computes less than half as many in prefill, because more prefixes stay cached. At concurrency 12, FP8 serves 1.5–1.6× the requests with 12–18× lower p95 TTFT and computes about a third as many prompt tokens in prefill. No preemptions in either arm. Pending: a prefix-caching-off control, and a run without our scheduler hook.

## Changes

- `ops/qsa.py`: one Triton helper, `_maybe_dequant`, chooses the decode by the cache tile's dtype: BF16 passes through, native e4m3 (sm_89+) upcasts to fp16, and `uint8` (the same e4m3 cache read as raw bytes below sm_89) is decoded with a bit cast (`2⁸` folded into the K/V scales on the host). Each K/V tile is decoded right after its load. On sm_80 FP8, 128-column / 4-warp tiles.
- `qsa.py`: on sm_89+ the uint8 cache is viewed as e4m3 once in `forward_qsa`; below sm_89 it stays `uint8`. Below sm_89 with FP8, skip the fused prepare/cache-write kernel (also an FP8 pointer); use the separate path.
- Byte decode: all 254 finite codes decode exactly (checked on A100, below). There is no CI test for it: CI has no sm_80 runner.

**Maintainer refactor (13 Oct, @gau-nernst, `a76baf2fd`…`3327e9bf1`), checked on A100.** It replaced the architecture flags with the dtype dispatch above, dropped the sm_80-only `[N, D]` + transpose K/V load, and interleaved load and dequant. On 1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, with the same synthetic reader inputs (2,048 selected tokens, TP8 geometry), the FP8 output is bitwise identical to the previous head at every row count, and all 254 finite codes decode exactly (the 2 NaN codes read as ±480, as before). FP8 kernel time, ms ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60602#issuecomment-6139631583)):

| Rows | Before (`210f422d9`) | Intermediate `71e77cf5e` (main's load/dequant order) | After (`6c9bc22f8`) | After ÷ before |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.156 | 0.148 | 0.150 | 0.96 |
| 32 | 0.179 | 0.171 | 0.171 | 0.95 |
| 80 | 0.250 | 0.285 | 0.247 | 0.99 |
| 128 | 0.298 | 0.366 | 0.296 | 0.99 |
| 512 | 0.724 | 0.951 | 0.730 | 1.01 |
| 1,024 | 1.312 | 1.866 | 1.307 | 1.00 |
| 2,048 | 1.991 | 3.002 | 1.989 | 1.00 |

BF16 is unchanged (0.98–1.02). The interleaved order matters on A100: with main's order the byte path is 12–51 % slower from 64 rows up. The serving results above were measured before the refactor; given bitwise-identical output and equal or lower kernel time, they still apply.

**NaN:** below sm_89 the two e4m3 NaN codes decode to ±480, as in vLLM's merged bit-cast FP8 decoders (Marlin FP8 on Ampere, #5975; CPU FP8 KV attention, #39445). A NaN-preserving decode costs 2.2× kernel time on A100, so it is not included. Details and a question for reviewers are under "NaN handling".

No new CPU/GPU sync. Validated outside CI (no A100 in CI). Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the submitter reviewed every line.

<details>
<summary>NaN handling</summary>

**What this PR does.** Below sm_89, the decode places the e4m3 sign, exponent and mantissa bits into an fp16 and folds `2⁸` into the scales. All 254 finite codes are exact. The two NaN codes (0x7F, 0xFF) decode to ±1.875 · 2⁸ = ±480. The cache can only hold a NaN code if a NaN was written: the CUDA cache writer uses `__nv_cvt_float_to_fp8(..., __NV_SATFINITE, ...)`, which saturates finite overflow to ±448.

**Merged vLLM precedents with the same behaviour:**

| Path | How FP8 is decoded | NaN codes become |
|---|---|---|
| Marlin FP8, Ampere weights (#5975, `csrc/.../marlin/dequant.h`) | bits placed into fp16/bf16 fields, bias by one multiply | finite (±480) |
| CPU FP8 KV attention, AMX/AVX-512 (#39445, `cpu_attn_amx.hpp`) | payload placed into a bf16 field, bias `2¹²⁰` folded into the K/V scales on the host, as here | finite (±480); its writer also clamps NaN input to ±448, so no NaN code is stored |
| ROCm FP8 weights (`w8a8_utils.py`, `fp8_utils.py`) | e4m3fn → e4m3fnuz | the fnuz NaN pattern is set to 0 |

TurboQuant (#38479) handles Ampere differently: it stores keys in Triton's `fp8e4b15`, so its cache format depends on the architecture. This PR keeps one e4m3 format on all architectures.

**What this kernel does with NaN today, on every architecture** (from the code): a NaN value element makes only that output element NaN. A NaN key makes the row's softmax normalizer NaN; `has_values = normalizer > 0` is then false and the row is written as zeros. So a NaN key is already not propagated on sm_89+.

**NaN-preserving decode, measured and not included.** We tried two variants on one A100 against this PR's kernel, on the same inputs:

| Variant | FP8 kernel time vs this PR (8 / 32 / 80 / 128 / 512 / 1,024 / 2,048 rows) |
|---|---|
| per-tile check of `byte & 0x7F` over K and V, NaN row at the end | 1.02 / 1.22 / 1.59 / 1.69 / 2.03 / 2.15 / 2.19 |
| branch-free decode (`(low + 1) & 0x80` sets the top fp16 exponent bit) | 1.00 / 1.26 / 1.62 / 1.86 / 2.26 / 2.25 / 2.35 |

**Question for reviewers:** is ±480 acceptable under the precedents above, or should NaN handling for this kernel be addressed for all architectures in a follow-up?

</details>

<details>
<summary>Decode cost</summary>

At concurrency 8 the BF16 cache does not limit anything, so this compares the decode cost of the two paths. Three runs per arm:

| | BF16 | FP8, this PR | Change (medians) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client TPOT p50 (Endpoints) | 8.1–8.2 ms | 8.6–8.7 ms | +6 % |
| Request inter-token latency, mean (`vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds`: time between a request's output events; with MTP one event can carry several tokens) | 24.4–25.6 ms | 25.3–25.5 ms | +2.9 % |
| MTP mean acceptance length per verification step (1 + accepted / drafts) | 2.73–2.75 | 2.68–2.72 | −0.9 % |
| MTP draft acceptance rate | 0.576–0.583 | 0.560–0.573 | −0.8 points |
| Mean decode time per request (`vllm:request_decode_time_seconds`) | 3.98–4.12 s | 3.97–4.11 s | no change |

- The vLLM values are means over each run's window of `/metrics` scrapes. The windows come from the client's session markers and are approximate.
- The MTP difference is small, and these runs do not establish its cause.
- At concurrency 16, the request inter-token latency is 38–39 ms with FP8 and 50–55 ms with BF16, where BF16 decode shares the batch with more prefill.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Duplicate check</summary>

Earlier attempts in this area (unmerged):
- #59943 (closed): byte decode for this kernel. The code owner asked whether FP8 KV on Ampere is needed and normally supported; the author had no deployment that reached this path and closed it. This PR adds the deployment data and the serving results.
- #60491 (closed by its author in favour of this PR): a new `fp8_e5m2` dtype for Ampere. The code owner asked why e5m2 instead of e4m3; this PR keeps e4m3.
- #54846 (open): e4m3 and NVFP4 for QSA; its FP8 part landed as #55557, which this PR extends below sm_89.

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "QSA fp8"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fp8e4nv"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Qwen4Exp sm80"
```

- **#60491** (closed by its author in favour of this PR after a side-by-side test on sm_86) added a new `fp8_e5m2` dtype for Ampere and makes `fp8_e4m3` fail early below sm_89. This PR keeps the existing `fp8_e4m3` instead:
  - no new dtype or flag;
  - 3 mantissa bits (e5m2 has 2);
  - one cache format read the same way on all architectures.

  This answers the reviewer question on #60491: "Is there a reason we should support e5m2 instead of just e4m3?"
- **#54846** (open) targets sm_120 (e4m3 and nvfp4) and does not cover sm_80.
- **#59943** (closed) is the earlier byte-decode attempt for this kernel. It used an `exp2` decode and 32-column tiles, and had no serving data.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests and kernel timing</summary>

**Environment:**
- 8× A100-SXM4-40GB (sm_80), driver 570.124.06, CUDA 12.9.
- vLLM `81198e97` (`0.31.1rc1.dev88+g81198e97b`, image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly-81198e97…`), with this PR's two files bound over the image's copies. Both files are byte-identical between 81198e97 and this PR's base.
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.3.

**Existing and new tests, one A100:**

```
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 55 | 60 |
| failed | 13 | 9 |
| errors | 6 | 6 |

- **Fixed:**
  - `test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_correctness[tp1_r1_fp8]`, `[tp1_r128_fp8]`, `[tp1_r2048_prefill_fp8]` and `[tp1_r2048_uniform_fp8]`, which fail on `main` with the error above;
  - the new 256-code decode test.
- **Unchanged:** the 9 FP8 *selection* failures (`test_qsa_decode_selection_correctness`, `test_qsa_prefill_selection_correctness`). They exercise the indexer, which stays BF16 and is not touched here.
- **The 6 errors** are a `workspace_init` out-of-memory on our shared test GPU, the same on both sides.

**Kernel time, one A100.** Synthetic paged cache: 1 KV head, 3 query heads, head dim 256, 2,048 selected keys per query row. Median of 24 CUDA-event samples, balanced launch order:

| Rows | BF16 cache (ms) | FP8 cache, this PR (ms) | FP8 / BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.160 | 0.169 | 1.05 |
| 32 | 0.176 | 0.181 | 1.03 |
| 80 | 0.219 | 0.250 | 1.14 |
| 128 | 0.321 | 0.296 | 0.92 |
| 512 | 0.763 | 0.724 | 0.95 |
| 1,024 | 1.361 | 1.307 | 0.96 |
| 2,048 | 2.571 | 2.462 | 0.96 |

**sm_80 FP8 launch retune.** Swept: BLOCK_N {32, 64, 128} × warps {1, 2, 4} × splits {1 … 64}. Every candidate was correctness-gated against a float64 reference, with max abs ≤ 0.02. FP8 / BF16 kernel time:

| Rows | Default table | Best candidate | This PR (128 / 4, table splits) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1.08 | 1.02 | 1.06 |
| 16 | 1.04 | 0.99 | 0.99 |
| 32 | 1.13 | 0.93 | 0.93 |
| 48 | 1.31 | 0.88 | 0.91 |
| 64 | 1.20 | 0.90 | 0.90 |
| 80 | 1.41 | 0.93 | 0.99 |
| 128 | 1.22 | 0.83 | 0.84 |
| 256 | 1.09 | 0.82 | 0.85 |

The default table was tuned for BF16 on GB300. One rule, 128 columns, 4 warps and the table's splits (capped at the 16 tiles of a 128-column launch), stays within 6 % of the best candidate at every row count. So this PR uses that rule instead of a per-row table.

**Coverage of the sweep:**
- Geometry: 1 KV head, 3 query heads, head dim 256, 2,048 selected columns. This is the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next shape per GPU at TP8.
- For rows above 64, the float64 check covers the first 64 rows; for 512/1,024/2,048 rows, the full output was checked separately.
- Other head counts and selection widths now take the same sm_80 FP8 launch but were not timed. Treat the rule as tuned for this geometry.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Accuracy details</summary>

**Accuracy, 8× A100, end to end: per-position prompt logprobs**, as in #55557. Three servers in sequence on the same image: BF16 (A), BF16 again (B, run-to-run noise) and FP8 with this PR's files. Same prompt token ids for every server, `prompt_logprobs=1`, temperature 0, prefix caching and MTP off, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-num-seqs 4`. For each position we take the logprob of the actual next prompt token and compare A with B (noise) and A with FP8.

| Prompt | Positions | σ of the difference, BF16 vs BF16 (nats) | σ, FP8 vs BF16 (nats) | Mean difference, FP8 vs BF16 | Positions off by > 1 nat, noise / FP8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agentic trajectories, 150k tokens | 149,999 | 0.111 | 0.115 | +0.0018 | 0.18 % / 0.21 % |
| Python source, 30k tokens | 29,999 | 0.062 | 0.074 | −0.0006 | 0.08 % / 0.13 % |
| Agentic text, 8k tokens | 7,999 | 0.402 | 0.417 | −0.024 | 3.08 % / 3.01 % |

- The FP8 deviation is close to the BF16 run-to-run noise on all three prompts (σ +4 %, +20 % and +4 %), with no systematic bias. Every position had a finite logprob in all three servers.
- KV pool in this configuration: BF16 1,405,504 / 1,405,900 tokens, FP8 2,633,776 tokens.
- A 125k-token needle check was also run. It gives no result: the BF16 servers do not retrieve the needle at any depth either (empty or wrong answers), so the check has no baseline. We do not count it.
- @nkuhn-vmw's GSM8K pairing on sm_86 (above) is the task-level check: FP8 92.65 / 91.74 against BF16 92.57 / 91.89, McNemar p = 1.00.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the accuracy trace</summary>

Each server runs alone on the 8 GPUs, one after another (BF16, BF16 again, FP8):

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --served-model-name flash-fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {bfloat16 | fp8}
```

Client steps (script below, sha256 `e8a77f55c7053dca05e7af47c0597c97b2feb96a3797f112900a6be271d957a2`):

```
python3 logprob_trace.py build   http://127.0.0.1:8000 out mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.jsonl   # once, on the first BF16 server
python3 logprob_trace.py run     http://127.0.0.1:8000 out bf16_a    # then bf16_b and fp8, each on its own server
python3 logprob_trace.py compare out bf16_a bf16_b fp8
```

- `build` tokenizes through the server's `/tokenize` and fixes the prompt token ids once. Every server then gets the same ids, and `compare` checks their hashes.
- Prompt sources: the official MLPerf agentic dataset (sha256 above), and the Python standard library inside the vLLM image (`/usr/lib/python3.12/*.py`, sorted) for the code prompt and the needle haystack.
- `run` sends each prompt to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens: 1, temperature: 0, prompt_logprobs: 1`. It keeps the logprob of the actual next prompt token at each position, and fails on a missing or non-finite value.
- `compare` reports, per prompt, the standard deviation and mean of the per-position difference, and the share of positions that differ by more than 1 nat.

```python
"""Per-position prompt-logprob trace and needle check against one running vLLM server (upstream #60602 evidence).

Method of vllm-project/vllm#55557: send identical prompt token ids with prompt_logprobs=1 at temperature 0, keep the
logprob of each actual next prompt token, and compare FP8-KV against BF16 with the BF16-vs-BF16 run-to-run noise as the
floor. Prompt ids are fixed once (build) and reused verbatim by every arm; each arm records the prompt hash it served.

This is a numerical diagnostic of the KV-cache dtype only (prefix caching and MTP off, eager). It is not a task-quality
or serving result. Every step fails loudly: a short source, a missing position or a non-finite logprob is an error.

  logprob_trace.py build   <base_url> <out_dir> <dataset.jsonl>
  logprob_trace.py run     <base_url> <out_dir> <arm>
  logprob_trace.py compare <out_dir> <arm_a> <arm_b> <arm_fp8>
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

MODEL = "flash-fp8"
TARGETS = {"agentic_150k": 150_000, "code_30k": 30_000, "text_8k": 8_000}
NEEDLE_TOKENS = 125_000
NEEDLE_DEPTHS = (0.1, 0.5, 0.9)
NEEDLE = "The secret passphrase for the archive is amber-falcon-42."
NEEDLE_ANSWER = "amber-falcon-42"
QUESTION = "\n\nQuestion: What is the secret passphrase for the archive? Answer: The secret passphrase is"
CODE_ROOT = Path("/usr/lib/python3.12")
METADATA_TYPE = "dataset_metadata"  # the full dataset's header row, skipped as MLCommons Endpoints does
REQUEST_SECONDS = 1500


def post(base, path, body):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=REQUEST_SECONDS) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())


def tokenize(base, text):
    return post(base, "/tokenize", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": text, "add_special_tokens": False})["tokens"]


def ids_sha256(ids):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(ids).encode()).hexdigest()


def write_private(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value))
    os.chmod(path, 0o600)


def code_text(limit_chars):
    parts, size = [], 0
    for path in sorted(CODE_ROOT.glob("*.py")):
        text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
        parts.append(text)
        size += len(text)
        if size >= limit_chars:
            return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"code source has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def agentic_text(dataset, limit_chars):
    """Messages of the longest conversations, as role-tagged text, until limit_chars."""
    conversations = {}
    for line in open(dataset):
        row = json.loads(line)
        if row.get("_type") == METADATA_TYPE:
            continue
        text = " ".join(str(row.get(key) or "") for key in ("content", "reasoning_content", "tool_calls"))
        conversations.setdefault(row["conversation_id"], []).append(f"[{row['role']}] {text}")
    parts, size = [], 0
    for conversation in sorted(conversations.values(), key=lambda c: -sum(map(len, c))):
        for message in conversation:
            parts.append(message)
            size += len(message)
            if size >= limit_chars:
                return "\n".join(parts)
    raise ValueError(f"dataset text has {size} characters, fewer than {limit_chars}")


def exactly(ids, count, name):
    if len(ids) < count:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: source gives {len(ids)} tokens, fewer than {count}")
    return ids[:count]


def build(base, out, dataset):
    out = Path(out)
    sources = {"agentic_150k": agentic_text(dataset, 1_200_000), "code_30k": code_text(300_000),
               "text_8k": agentic_text(dataset, 80_000)}
    prompts = {name: exactly(tokenize(base, sources[name]), TARGETS[name], name) for name in TARGETS}
    needle, question = tokenize(base, " " + NEEDLE + " "), tokenize(base, QUESTION)
    body = NEEDLE_TOKENS - len(needle) - len(question)
    haystack = exactly(tokenize(base, code_text(1_200_000)), body, "haystack")
    needles, positions = {}, {}
    for depth in NEEDLE_DEPTHS:
        name, at = f"needle_{int(depth * 100)}", int(body * depth)
        needles[name] = haystack[:at] + needle + haystack[at:] + question
        positions[name] = at
    write_private(out / "prompts.json", {"trace": prompts, "needle": needles})
    summary = {"lengths": {k: len(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}, "needle_positions": positions,
               "sha256": {k: ids_sha256(v) for k, v in {**prompts, **needles}.items()}}
    write_private(out / "prompts-summary.json", summary)
    print(json.dumps(summary["lengths"]))


def trace(base, ids, name):
    result = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0,
                                            "prompt_logprobs": 1})
    choice, usage = result["choices"][0], result.get("usage") or {}
    rows = choice["prompt_logprobs"]
    if len(rows) != len(ids) or usage.get("prompt_tokens") != len(ids):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(rows)} logprob rows, usage {usage.get('prompt_tokens')}, sent {len(ids)}")
    values = []
    for position in range(1, len(ids)):
        chosen = (rows[position] or {}).get(str(ids[position]))
        if chosen is None or not math.isfinite(chosen["logprob"]):
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: no finite logprob for the prompt token at position {position}")
        values.append(chosen["logprob"])
    return values, {"usage": usage, "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason")}


def run(base, out, arm):
    out = Path(out)
    prompts = json.loads((out / "prompts.json").read_text())
    record = {"arm": arm, "trace": {}, "needle": {}, "seconds": {}, "api": {}, "sha256": {}}
    for name, ids in prompts["trace"].items():
        start = time.time()
        record["trace"][name], record["api"][name] = trace(base, ids, name)
        record["seconds"][name], record["sha256"][name] = time.time() - start, ids_sha256(ids)
    for name, ids in prompts["needle"].items():
        answer = post(base, "/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0})
        choice = answer["choices"][0]
        record["needle"][name] = {"text": choice["text"], "found": NEEDLE_ANSWER in choice["text"],
                                  "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason"), "usage": answer.get("usage")}
        record["sha256"][name] = ids_sha256(ids)
    write_private(out / f"{arm}.json", record)
    print(json.dumps({"arm": arm, "needle": {k: v["found"] for k, v in record["needle"].items()},
                      "seconds": record["seconds"]}))


def spread(first, second, name):
    if len(first) != len(second):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {len(first)} and {len(second)} positions differ")
    diffs = [b - a for a, b in zip(first, second)]
    mean = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    sigma = math.sqrt(sum((d - mean) ** 2 for d in diffs) / len(diffs))
    return {"positions": len(diffs), "sigma_nat": round(sigma, 4), "mean_nat": round(mean, 5),
            "share_over_1_nat": round(sum(abs(d) > 1 for d in diffs) / len(diffs), 5)}


def compare(out, arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8):
    out = Path(out)
    a, b, f = (json.loads((out / f"{x}.json").read_text()) for x in (arm_a, arm_b, arm_fp8))
    if not a["sha256"] == b["sha256"] == f["sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("arms served different prompt ids")
    table = {name: {"bf16_noise": spread(a["trace"][name], b["trace"][name], name),
                    "fp8_vs_bf16": spread(a["trace"][name], f["trace"][name], name)} for name in a["trace"]}
    table["needle"] = {arm["arm"]: {k: v["found"] for k, v in arm["needle"].items()} for arm in (a, b, f)}
    write_private(out / "compare.json", table)
    print(json.dumps(table, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"build": build, "run": run, "compare": compare}[sys.argv[1]](*sys.argv[2:])
```

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary>Serving details</summary>

- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, context 262,144, MTP 3, prefix caching, `--max-num-batched-tokens 1024`.
- vLLM 81198e97 with this PR's two files bound over the image copies, against the same image unmodified. Only `--kv-cache-dtype` differs between the arms.
- Client: MLCommons Endpoints [`594612e6`](https://github.com/mlcommons/endpoints/commit/594612e61b6f5bf0a237cba473244113bdbb49c2), unmodified, streaming. It replays the full recorded agentic dataset: 613 multi-turn coding conversations (20,297 assistant turns, prompts up to about 200k tokens), with recorded tool delays between turns. Concurrency is Endpoints' `target_concurrency`: the number of conversations in flight, each with at most one open request. Each run issues new turns for 1 hour, then drains. Three runs per arm.

<details>
<summary>Exact serving setup (both arms)</summary>

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --cudagraph-capture-sizes 1 2 4 8 16 24 32 40 48 56 64 96 128 192 256 384 512 768 1024 1536 2048 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16"}' \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {bfloat16 | fp8}
```

- Environment: `VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=1`, `VLLM_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.9/compat` (host driver older than the image CUDA).
- **Not stock vLLM, in both arms:**
  - A `sitecustomize` hook replaces `EngineCore._should_throttle_prefills`: with DP1, new prefills are admitted only on every 16th scheduler step while requests are running, unless a prefill chunk is already running. Continuing prefill chunks are not delayed. It changes no model or kernel code.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Slice expert LoRA by the unpadded per-rank size under TP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Expert LoRA factors are sliced at the wrong offset under TP > 1 when the MoE backend pads the expert intermediate dimension (e.g. Marlin / FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4). Every rank except rank 0 silently applies the wrong LoRA rows.

## Claims

- `FusedMoEWithLoRA` and `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` shard an adapter along the intermediate dim by the unpadded per-rank size, matching how the base expert weights are sharded.
- No behavior change when the backend does not pad.
- No dependency on a FlashInfer version.

## Validation

CPU-only check of the slicing (TP 2 and 4, every rank, per-expert and both 3D layouts, padded and unpadded), run locally and not added to the test suite:

| `vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py` | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 6 (unpadded cases) | 6 (padded cases) |
| this PR | 12 | 0 |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed file.

End-to-end on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, TP 2, `moe_backend="marlin"` (per-rank intermediate size 1440 padded to 1536), random expert-only LoRA (rank 8, seeded; `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`). Reference: the same model at TP 1 with `triton_unfused`, which does no TP slicing. 16 prompts x 200 tokens, teacher-forced `prompt_logprobs`. Nightly arm64 image at `af7f9488c` (the changed file is byte-identical to `ffec22127` there), one run per row:

| TP 2 marlin | adapter | MAE vs ref | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | none | 0.150 | – | – |
| `main` | small | 0.444 | 0.38 | 0.47 |
| `main` | large | 1.682 | 0.53 | 0.50 |
| this PR | none | 0.157 | – | – |
| this PR | small | 0.139 | 0.76 | 0.82 |
| this PR | large | 1.013 | 0.83 | 0.77 |

`triton_unfused` at TP 2 is affected as well (1440 padded to 1472): small adapter 0.444 on `main`, 0.144 with this PR (no-adapter floor 0.137).

The no-adapter rows are the Marlin-vs-Triton floor (Marlin differs from itself by 0.09 across two runs). With this change the small adapter is back at that floor; the projection of the adapter effect (logprob with adapter minus base) on the reference effect goes from 0.38 to 0.76. The large adapter degrades the model itself (Marlin self-difference 0.69), so only the direction is meaningful there.

The same on/off contrast on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, 576 padded to 640, FlashInfer TRTLLM experts with a prototype LoRA path, change backported to an older dev build): MAE against the unpadded Triton backend 0.028 -> 0.014 for a small adapter (no-adapter floor 0.014) and 0.73 -> 0.31 for a large one.

## Details

Root cause: `_slice_w13_b` / `_slice_w2_a` use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition` as the per-rank stride. `RoutedExperts.__init__` overwrites that field with the result of `maybe_roundup_sizes()`, so it is the padded size (MXFP4 rounds up to 128 for Marlin / TRTLLM / DeepGEMM / CUTLASS and to 64 for Triton). The base weights are sharded by `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size` in `RoutedExperts._load_w13` / `_load_w2`. With 576 padded to 640, the base weight of rank `r` holds rows `[576 r, 576 (r + 1))` while the adapter slice is `[640 r, 640 (r + 1))`. Nothing raises because the slice is copied into the head of a zero buffer. We first observed this on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, padded MoE backends).

Fix: use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` as the stride. Buffers keep the padded size with a zero tail. For the concatenated `(gate, up)` layout of the 3D class, the up half is placed at the allocated per-rank size, where the base `w13` has it.

Not addressed: GPT-OSS MXFP4 uses a block-aligned shard stride in its own loader (`cdiv(intermediate_size / 32, tp_size) * 32`), which differs from `intermediate_size // tp_size` at TP 4 / 8.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs and issues for `_slice_w13_b`, `intermediate_size_per_partition LoRA padded`, `fused_moe LoRA TP slice`; nothing addresses this. #61164 and #61165 touch other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | median ITL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` + `1e1842a` | 2968 (2962–2974) | 18.73 ms | 12.80 ms |
| this PR | 2946 (2928–2958) | 18.89 ms | 12.94 ms |

The ~0.8% gap matches the two extra small kernels per indexer layer on SM100 (weights → BF16, row-aware logits → FP32, ~3 µs together). Feeding BF16 straight from the Q producers and into a BF16 top-k removes both.

**Unit tests** (GB200):

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                      # 7 passed (SM100 MX + varlen paths)
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_*.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_glm5next_indexer_block_sizes.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_*.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
                                                                               # 558 passed, 35 skipped
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py                      # 222 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py                                 # all passed
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k deep_gemm
                                                                               # 100 passed, 169 skipped
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # now also imports the package
```

`tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` fails on this GB200 with `unspecified launch failure` identically on `main` + `1e1842a` (pre-existing, unrelated). Not run (no hardware): SM90 and SM120; CI's H100 DeepGEMM job covers the SM90 attention tests. CI has no SM100 DeepGEMM job, so the MX path is validated only by the runs above.

**Pin delta `1448881` → `6ce1c5e`**: the end-to-end runs above used `1448881`. The two later commits change no kernel math (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33 only lowers the host and device stride asserts, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 only module naming). Re-checked on `6ce1c5e` on GB200 (the GPUs were shared with another job, so no end-to-end rerun):

```
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # imports; init takes the package name
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
                                                                               # 42 passed, 7 skipped (need pip deep_gemm)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "deep_gemm or deepgemm"
                                                                               # 125 passed, 28 skipped
# DeepGEMM's tests/test_attention.py::test_sparse_mqa_logits, paged cases only, on the vendored build:
# 60/60 passed with 64-token pages of 8448 B (MXFP8) / 4352 B (MXFP4), 256- but not 512-aligned
```

## Details

- `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` now passes `--force` to `setup.py build_ext`. DeepGEMM's `setup.py` lists only `csrc/python_api.cpp`, so after a pin change that touched only headers (`config.hpp` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) an incremental build silently kept the old extension and the import failed with `deep_gemm::init() expected at most 1 argument(s)`. CMake already reruns this step on DeepGEMM header changes and `python_api.cpp` is the only translation unit, so forcing adds no work.
- Why not duplicate: no open PR bumps DeepGEMM past `1e1842a` or adapts the indexer to the new MQA API (#59503 bumps to an older SM107 fix already contained in the current pin; #59482 is the Stable ABI migration).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][DCP] Support a2a DCP comm backend for FlashMLA sparse
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`FlashMLASparseMetadataBuilder` rejects any DCP comm backend other than `ag_rs`. 
The mixed-batch fp8 path already returns `(out, lse)` for every MQA token, with packed heads and with rows that have no local top-k candidates set to `(0, -inf)`. That is the input `MLADCPManager`'s `a2a` combine expects, both the direct symmetric-memory kernel and the NCCL all-to-all fallback for batches larger than the direct workspace. This PR removes the guard.

PCP + DCP still requires `ag_rs`. The MRV2 PCP manager enforces that (`MRV2 PCP + DCP requires dcp_comm_backend='ag_rs'`), and PCP is MRV2-only.

With `ag_rs`, each layer's combine is an NCCL all-gather of the LSEs plus a reduce-scatter of the outputs, which means many small NCCL kernels per decode step. With `a2a` it is one exchange per layer.

There is also a side effect for GLM-5.x: `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` defaults DCP to `a2a`, so with this change it no longer fails at startup when FlashMLA sparse serves DCP (`--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, or SM90).

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and merged PRs for `dcp a2a flashmla`, `dcp_comm_backend`, `FlashMLA sparse DCP`, `decode context parallel symmetric memory`, `dcp a2a`, `flashmla sparse a2a`:
- #59310 fixes the same startup failure from the other side: it keeps GLM DSA's DCP defaults on `ag_rs` wherever FlashMLA sparse serves DCP. Its description mentions lifting the guard as the alternative but leaves it alone because it was not validated. This PR is that alternative, with validation below. If this PR lands, #59310's Hopper/forced-backend fallback is no longer needed.
- #54472 and #60373 change direct-A2A layout handling (strided output and LSE). FlashMLA sparse already hands the combine packed heads (the fp8 kernel's LSE is token-major; checked on SM100), so this PR does not depend on either one.
- #46514 added the guard. Nothing else touches it.

## Test Plan / Results

Unit tests (GB300):
```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dcp     # 7 passed (incl. new test_fp8_dcp_accepts_comm_backend[ag_rs|a2a])
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py
# 44 passed, 12 failed -- the same 12 fail on unmodified main (test-side dtype/mock/query_start_loc issues), unrelated to this change
```

Combine precision check (4x GB300, 64 heads, D=512, T=40, rows empty on some ranks set to `(0, -inf)`), measured against an fp32 LSE-weighted reference: the direct a2a combine has max error 0.010-0.013 and mean 0.0009. The ag_rs path (correct_attn_out followed by a bf16 reduce-scatter) has max error 0.026-0.032 and mean 0.0015. No NaNs in either.

End-to-end setup: `zai-org/GLM-5.3` (FP8) on 2x4 GB300, TP8, `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. Default runner (MRV2), FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs. The DCP runs add `--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --no-dcp-q-replicate` and either `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` or `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`. The log confirms `Using direct symmetric-memory DCP A2A for MLA.`

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-tokens 512`, 5-shot):

| config | accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.918 |
| TP8 + DCP8 ag_rs | 0.917 |
| TP8 + DCP8 a2a | 0.914 |

Prompt logprobs on 3 fixed texts (115 positions, mean abs diff): a2a vs TP8 0.065, ag_rs vs TP8 0.058. For comparison, TP8 against itself under different concurrent load gives 0.073. Greedy outputs are identical run to run for a given config.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos`, a different seed per point, mean TTFT/TPOT in ms:

| point | TP8 | DCP8 ag_rs | DCP8 a2a | a2a vs ag_rs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 8k, c1 (TTFT) | 541 | 923 | 867 | -6% |
| prefill 32k, c1 (TTFT) | 2193 | 3653 | 3433 | -6% |
| decode 1k/256, c1 (TPOT) | 9.50 | 15.17 | 13.45 | -11% |
| decode 1k/256, c16 (TPOT) | 15.71 | 23.28 | 20.84 | -10% |
| decode 1k/256, c64 (TPOT) | 27.35 | 38.83 | 34.97 | -10% |
| decode 32k/256, c1 (TPOT) | 9.59 | 14.84 | 13.10 | -12% |

DCP8 holds 21.95M KV tokens versus 2.75M for TP8 (8x).

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Clef-Flash support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add native support for [Cloudflare/clef-flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash) through `/v1/systemone`, reusing the Qwen3.5 backbone and the joint schema head introduced for Clef-Omni in #61064.

## Claims

- Automatically detect and load the separate joint schema head, scoring `choice`, `noul`, and `score` questions in one pooling request.
- Support text/JSON, images, and videos sampled at 2 fps. Match the release's fixed prompt, media separators, schema spans, and 16K truncation.
- Share the head/pooler between Clef-Flash and Clef-Omni. Flash rejects audio inputs and ignores video soundtracks.

## Validation

Compared the full checkpoint at revision `8b2e5fd17c09fd49bc2880b805d5323ec7ff4ff3` against the release's `joint_schema_model.py` in BF16. Ten model inputs covered invoice decisions, Unicode/empty instructions, a state truncated to 16K, one/two images, video, and image+video. Prompt token IDs and question/option spans matched the reference exactly in all ten cases.

Each mode ran the ten inputs once sequentially and twice at concurrency 4:

| Mode | Requests | Highest-probability option matches | Max absolute probability difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eager | 30 | 57/57 | 0.001508 |
| Default compile | 30 | 57/57 | 0.000863 |

The four invoice threshold labels were correct in every repetition (12/12 per mode). These are synthetic model correctness checks. Probability normalization and input-token counts also matched; output-token counts were zero.

The reference evaluation used `encode_record`, `collate_records`, and `load_release_model(..., attn_implementation="sdpa")`, comparing each question's softmax probabilities against `/v1/systemone` responses. Serve the model with:

```bash
vllm serve Cloudflare/clef-flash \
  --served-model-name clef-flash --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 8
# Add --enforce-eager for the eager comparison.
```

## Details

The checkpoint advertises `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and supplies `joint_head_config.json` plus `joint_head.safetensors`. Architecture conversion detects that head, and the Flash wrapper uses the output embedding table for lexical option features, matching the reference implementation.

The existing Clef head/pooler is moved unchanged into `clef_joint_schema.py`. Flash shares the joint schema strategy's typed answers and span/truncation logic, with its own media rendering for adjacent placeholders and a single trailing newline.

Duplicate checks found no open Clef-Flash support PR. #61064 supports Clef-Omni; the other open Clef-related PRs concern API/frontend behavior.

Model comparisons cover BF16 with TP=1. Multi-GPU configurations, quantization, and the full Clef checkpoint were not evaluated.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement and validate this model support.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip redundant sparse index remap on non-indexer layers
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

## Update: indexer and non-indexer layers are two KV cache groups

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781  added the is_index_group_leader field to MLAAttentionSpec: `is_index_group_leader=self.indexer is not None,`. Layers can only share a KV cache group if they agree on is_index_group_leader, so once the flag is set per layer, indexer and non-indexer layers land in different groups and therefore get different metadata instances with separate paged_kv_indices

```
index_group_leader_set = {spec.is_index_group_leader for spec in specs}
assert (
    ...
    and len(index_group_leader_set) == 1
    ...
), (
    "All attention layers in the same KV cache group must use the same "
    "... index-sharing role, ..."
)
```

So, remap should run for all indexer layers and the first non-indexer layer. The two non-indexer layer following the first non-indexer layer doesn't need a remap.

The following table shows how the remap condition changed between the commits and how it is implemented by `index_epoch` and  `remapped_epoch`. index_epoch is fixed per layer at construction: it counts indexer writes up to and including that layer - which selection is this layer entitled to read. remapped_epoch lives on the metadata and moves during the pass: it records which selection is currently sitting in that group's paged_kv_indices. A mismatch means the group is holding an older selection and must refresh.

| Layer | Owns indexer | Group | `index_epoch` | group's `remapped_epoch` before | Commit 1 | Commit 2 | group's remapped_epoch after |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| 0 | yes | A | 1 | -1 | remap | remap | 1 |
| 1 | yes | A | 2 | 1 | remap | remap | 2 |
| 2 | yes | A | 3 | 2 | remap | remap | 3 |
| 3 | no | B | 3 | -1 | skip | remap | 3 |
| 4 | no | B | 3 | 3 | skip | skip | 3 |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip cleaning sparse prefill MQA logits
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.
This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel.

This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty`
and the fill is removed.

## Safety

The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside
`[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial
load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged.

## Results

MI355X, TP=4, rank 0, comparable before/after captures:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP32 fill launches | 18,162 | **0** |
| FP32 fill GPU time | 1,250.2 ms | **0 ms** |
| MQA-logits launches | 18,108 | 17,930 |

The removed fill was **0.89% of total GPU kernel time**. In the sample below it
takes 74.6 µs and is fully serialized before the logits kernel.
