commits.pr_title: [CI] Pace the CRCR nightly report under the relay rate limit
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The torch-nightly CRCR report (`.buildkite/scripts/crcr_report.py`) posts one callback per Buildkite job, back to back, with no retry. The PyTorch Cross-Repo CI Relay limits callbacks per repo over a sliding 60 s window (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, currently 100). So every nightly records only the first 100 jobs and the rest get a 429:

| Build | Report |
|---|---|
| [93355](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93355) | `reported 100 job(s), 244 failed` |
| [93593](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93593) | `reported 100 job(s), 269 failed` |
| [93820](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93820) | `reported 100 job(s), 270 failed` |

```
429 for :nvidia: (H100) MLA Kernel Test: {"detail": "rate limit exceeded for vllm-project/vllm"}
```

HUD's CRCR view of vLLM nightlies therefore covers about 27% of the jobs, and which jobs depends on the order Buildkite returns them in. The step is `soft_fail` and exits 0, so nothing flagged it.

## Changes

- **`crcr_report.py`:** wait `CRCR_POST_INTERVAL_S` (default 0.65 s, about 92/min, under the current limit) between callbacks. Retry a 429 with 2/4/8/16/32 s backoff, about 62 s in total so the last attempt lands in a fresh window. A full nightly (~370 jobs) now takes about 4 minutes to report.
- **`crcr-report.sh`:** the post-wait OIDC token is minted with `--lifetime 1800`, because the default five-minute lifetime no longer covers a paced report. If the agent rejects `--lifetime`, it falls back to the old call, so the report is never lost to a flag mismatch.

Relay side: pytorch/test-infra#9096 raises the limit to 300/min/repo and adds the same 429 retry to the GitHub Actions reporter. Once that is deployed, `CRCR_POST_INTERVAL_S` can be lowered.

## Test Plan

Ran `crcr_report.py` against a local fake relay:
- Responses 200, 429, 429, then 200: the second job retried after 2 s and 4 s, and all 4 jobs were reported (`reported 4 job(s), 0 failed`).
- 429 every time, with backoff shortened: every job was logged as `429 for …` after its retries, `reported 0 job(s), 4 failed`, exit 0 (best-effort, unchanged).

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `bash -n` and `shellcheck` are clean.

## Test Result

The next torch-nightly run (`TORCH_NIGHTLY=1` on main) should log `reported <all> job(s), 0 failed` for the CRCR step.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Gemma AR+RMS prefill fallback
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

1. Teach the AITER compilation pass to preserve raw Gemma weights and pass `gemma_norm` through the fused all-reduce op.
2. When custom all-reduce rejects a large prefill tensor, run the regular all-reduce followed by AITER's fused-add RMSNorm (the registered `vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm` op, which gains a `gemma_norm` flag) instead of decomposing the norm into fp32 pointwise and reduction kernels. Keep Gemma inputs out of the QuickReduce fused RMSNorm path, which has no weight-bias mode.

On main alone, large prefill does not reach this fallback, so the speedup only shows up together with #57547, which sends prefill above the custom all-reduce pool through it.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
- Base: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7`, each arm adds only the PRs listed; empty compile caches per run
- Serving A/B: ISL=60000, OSL=600, concurrency `{4, 32, 128}`, range-ratio=1.0
- Accuracy: GPQA diamond, 198 problems, thinking on, temperature=1.0, top-p=0.95, top-k=20, max-tokens=100000, num-threads=32. Same servers as the serving A/B.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py` — Gemma prefill that misses 1-stage fused AR+RMS goes through regular all-reduce then `fused_add_rms_norm(..., gemma_norm=True)`, and never enters fused QR+RMSNorm
  - `tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py` — Gemma variants of the AR+RMS fusion tests; fused graph matches the unfused Gemma residual path

---

## Test Result

### Unit tests

Hardware: 2× MI355X, this PR's diff applied to the nightly above.

```bash
python -m pytest -v --tb=short \
  tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py \
  tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py \
  -k "gemma_rmsnorm_falls_back or Gemma"
```

```text
7 passed, 4 skipped
```

### Performance

Median TTFT and output throughput.

#### This PR on main

| Cell | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 5954 ms | 5733 ms | −3.7% | 109.5 | 109.4 | −0.1% |
| c=32 | 5513 ms | 5534 ms | +0.4% | 163.4 | 159.4 | −2.5% |
| c=128 | 158478 ms | 158404 ms | 0.0% | 176.1 | 176.0 | −0.1% |

Neutral, as expected: on main the 8k prefill chunks never reach the fallback.

#### With #57547: fallback norm as separate fp32 kernels vs this PR

| Cell | TTFT before | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s before | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 7035 ms | 5423 ms | **−22.9%** | 95.7 | 113.0 | **+18.1%** |
| c=32 | 6795 ms | 5266 ms | **−22.5%** | 131.8 | 169.1 | **+28.3%** |
| c=128 | 195683 ms | 151098 ms | **−22.8%** | 143.0 | 184.3 | **+28.9%** |

The separate kernels take about 0.75 ms per call against about 0.09 ms for the fused kernel. With 185 calls per 8k prefill chunk, that is about 120 ms of a roughly 550 ms prefill step, which matches the TTFT change.

#### main vs main + #57547 + this PR

| Cell | TTFT main | TTFT both | Δ | tok/s main | tok/s both | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 5954 ms | 5423 ms | **−8.9%** | 109.5 | 113.0 | **+3.3%** |
| c=32 | 5513 ms | 5266 ms | **−4.5%** | 163.4 | 169.1 | **+3.5%** |
| c=128 | 158478 ms | 151098 ms | **−4.7%** | 176.1 | 184.3 | **+4.6%** |

### Accuracy

GPQA diamond, 198 problems, thinking on, temperature=1.0, top-p=0.95, top-k=20, max-tokens=100000, num-threads=32.

| main | this PR | #57547, separate fp32 norm | #57547 + this PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 92.4% (183/198) | 92.4% (183/198) | 91.9% (182/198) | 92.4% (183/198) |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Omit unset sampling params in render output
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust render sends `null` for every unset sampling field and Python `/inference/v1/generate` rejects them. This skips serializing `None` so Rust render output can go straight into Python generate. 

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions/render` on the Rust frontend no longer emits `null` in `sampling_params`
- Rust render → Python generate works for requests that leave float fields like `temperature` or `top_p` unset which is nearly every request

## Validation

Before, a minimal chat render returned:

    "sampling_params": {"temperature": null, "top_p": null, "max_tokens": 64, "watermarking": true, ...}

After, the null keys are gone.

Tests added:
- `sampling_params_serialization_omits_unset_fields` (`vllm-text` unit test, includes a round trip)
- `render_chat_omits_unset_sampling_params` (`vllm-server` route test)
- `test_rust_render_sampling_params_without_nulls_validate` (Python test for a body without nulls validates, `"temperature": null` is rejected)

## Details

`vllm_text::SamplingParams` has `Option` fields but no `skip_serializing_none`. The attribute on `GenerateSamplingParams` doesn't reach the flattened inner struct, so the nulls leaked out.

- `watermarking: true` is still emitted. It isn't an `Option` and Python treats `None` and `True` the same
- Nested `structured_outputs` and `repetition_detection` don't emit nulls, so they needed no change
- No schema change. Unset fields come back as `None` through `#[serde(default)]`

No existing PR covers this (checked open PRs for "skip_serializing_none sampling" and "Rust render null sampling_params").

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Check multimodal chunk boundaries before encoder cache reuse
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Apply the existing `disable_chunked_mm_input` boundary guard before warm encoder-cache hits and same-step image deduplication can bypass it. Related to #52306; this addresses a separate cache-hit failure from #52412's equality-boundary fix.

## Claims

- Cached and same-step duplicate images obey the same existing no-chunking guard as uncached images.
- Preserve encoder reuse without changing the guard predicate, EAGLE shift arithmetic, configuration, or public API.
- Add regressions to the existing CPU scheduler suite. No performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

### Independently rerun CPU checks

On upstream base `e5d33a36e71da9e3e122ac9b139f3ab3b944ef71`, with Python 3.12 and CPU PyTorch 2.13:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

Result: **241 passed**. The focused command uses `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k test_no_mm_input_chunking -q`: **2 failed, 1 passed** with the original scheduler; **3 passed** with the patch. Original warm-cache scheduling ends at 1024 instead of 400; same-step dedup ends at 1024 instead of 776. These tests run in the existing Buildkite CPU-core step.

Eleven relevant pre-commit hooks, the Python 3.10/3.12 mypy hooks, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. The aggregate pre-commit command was attempted but its unrelated actionlint environment could not install because the available Go executable rejects `install`; applicable hooks were run individually.

### Human-submitter GPU validation

The following results come from my GPU validation summary on base `47de9d4d049831914858404c48827837c2d915db`, using the same patch. The assistant reviewed the summary and checked patch correspondence; it did not independently run these GPU tests or inspect their raw logs. After syncing upstream, the encoder-scheduling method, Gemma3 model, Triton backend, and encoder cache manager remain unchanged; GPU tests were not repeated on the newer base.

Environment: WSL2/Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.4, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (12227 MiB). Model: `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it`, revision `bf46152c47f5dd20b896357cb51abc4c03b8ee8c`, BF16, Triton attention, one request at a time, 512-token scheduling budget. Decoder prefix caching and speculative decoding were disabled; image-content hashing remained enabled.

Eight red/blue-image requests covered cold/warm encoder caches, different text prefixes, and repeated images within one prompt. Traces confirmed actual encoder reuse.

| Check | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image splits across eight requests | 4 | 0 |
| First-step end, warm image `[336,596)` | 512 | 336 |
| First-step end, second repeated image `[437,697)` | 512 | 437 |
| Warm-image hidden-state cosine against full-prefill reference | ~0.798–0.799 | ~0.988–0.990 |
| Second repeated-image cosine | ~0.822–0.830 | ~0.980 |

Patched minimum cosine was 0.98610 over the full sequence and 0.98017 over image spans. Seven of eight reported generation comparisons were token-identical; the red cold request differed in punctuation (`Red.` versus `Red`). This is not a claim of universal output identity.

The existing `test_mm_prefix_lm_e2e` in `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py` also passed (**1 passed**) with its original pan-and-scan setting and 0.9 assertions, using the local checkpoint, Triton, and 2 GB CPU offload: full-sequence cosine 0.91150, image cosine 0.90925. An additional exploratory 0.99 threshold was not met in all cases.

## Details

Both cache fast paths previously returned before the boundary guard. Reusing encoder embeddings does not supply decoder K/V for the image under a different text prefix, so cache state must not bypass the decoder-span policy. The fix relocates the existing guard intact; the shared scheduler path serves both model runners.

Tradeoff: a cached image can now wait for sufficient decoder-token budget. Deferred items are not prematurely pinned; an invalid cached embedding-count mismatch may be reported when the item is admitted instead.

Duplicate checks on 2026-10-02 covered #52306 and its comments, #52412's patch/discussion, and open/merged PRs for the flag and cache/chunking keywords. No existing guard-order fix was found. #52412 changes `<` to `<=`; this PR preserves `<`, and that equality-only change still permits the cache-hit bypass. #59330 changes the P/D prompt-end bound, not these fast paths.

Limits: equality-boundary and prefix-cache mid-item behavior are unchanged. Existing EAGLE rollback arithmetic can still split an adjacent image (for example `[100,300)`, `[300,500)`, shift 1, budget 400 rolls back to 299). This PR does not fix that; GPU validation did not enable EAGLE. HTTP load, production-duration workloads, other attention backends, and quantization were not validated.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and PR preparation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the relevant tests, including the GPU validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor request_id and X-Request-Id in chat and completions render
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python render now uses the caller's `request_id` / `X-Request-Id` for chat and completions instead of always minting a random one.

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/messages/render` return `chatcmpl-{id}` where `id` is the `X-Request-Id` header, else the body `request_id`, else a random UUID
- `/v1/completions/render` returns `cmpl-{id}` for one prompt and `cmpl-{id}-{i}` for several
- Requests that send no ID behave as before

## Validation

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py`:

- body ID is honored
- header beats body
- random IDs are unique across calls
- single-prompt completions
- multi-prompt completions with the suffix

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -v
```

## Details

Rust render and the coupled chat path already honor both the header and the body field. Python render didn't, so an ID couldn't be followed across render, generate and derender. I reused `BaseServing._base_request_id`, so the precedence matches the coupled path.

For multi-prompt completions I only add the `-{i}` suffix when there is more than one prompt. That keeps a single prompt equal to Rust's `cmpl-{id}`. The coupled `OpenAIServingCompletion` always appends `-{i}`, so this differs slightly from it.

`raw_request` is optional on the render methods, so the Cohere and Anthropic callers and the coupled paths are unchanged. Responses render is untouched.

No duplicate: I searched open PRs for render request ID handling and found nothing.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Make the sparse MLA prefill workspace size configurable
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor`. It replaces the fixed `5 * max_model_len` FlashMLA sparse prefill workspace and the `40 * max_model_len` DSA indexer prefill buffer sized from it. Unset, `VllmConfig` resolves it to 5 up to a 256K `max_model_len` and to 2 above. At a 1M `max_model_len` the fixed reservations hold several GiB per GPU that a long-context deployment can return to the KV cache.

Related: #60874 (right-sizes the DeepSeek-V4.1 copies of these buffers), #42856 (fixed lower factors on SM120 only), #59319 (skips the FlashMLA workspace on the fp8 mixed-batch path).

## Claims

- Up to a 256K `max_model_len` the default keeps every size identical to main.
- Above 256K the default is 2: workspace `2 * max_model_len`, indexer `16 * max_model_len`. `--attention-config.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=5` restores the main sizes.
- The default resolves once, in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`. KV cache auto-fit can lower `max_model_len` after the workspace is reserved, so a factor derived later could switch from 2 to 5 and size a step past the reservation.
- One knob sizes both buffers. The indexer buffer stays `(576 * 2 // 132) * factor` rows, so it still fits inside the FlashMLA workspace.
- Both chunkers keep each request's context in one gather, so a lower factor changes only how many requests share a gather.
- The floor is 2 (`ge=2`). Under PCP+DCP the per-rank budget is `factor * max_model_len // dcp`, and a full-length request's shard can round up past `max_model_len // dcp`, which `split_prefill_chunks` asserts against.
- GLM-5.3 FP8 on H100 at a 1M `max_model_len` (PCP8, DCP8, TP1): factor 2 raises available KV cache from 9.07 to 18.36 GiB per GPU.

## Validation

**Default, CPU.** On 06a24c32f, a real `VllmConfig` (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, CPU device) resolves the factor and both buffer sizes as follows:

| `max_model_len` | factor | workspace | indexer |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 163840 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262144 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262145 | 2 | 2x | 16x |
| 1048576 | 2 | 2x | 16x |

An explicit factor of 3 at 1M is kept, and `AttentionConfig(sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=1)` raises a validation error. `test_indexer_prefill_budget_matches_compressed_workspace` reads the resolved factor through `create_vllm_config`; it needs a GPU, so CI runs it in the `v1/attention` job. pre-commit (ruff, mypy, `validate-config`, test tethering) passes on the changed files.

**GLM-5.3 on H100, same sizes.** We run GLM-5.3 FP8 in production with these exact sizes (workspace 2x, indexer 16x) applied to the same two functions on our vLLM build. The prefill engines are PCP8, DCP8, TP1, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 64, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.

| | factor 5 | factor 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache per GPU | 9.07 GiB | 18.36 GiB |
| KV cache tokens per 8-GPU engine | 1.40M to 1.42M | 2.63M to 2.88M |
| 1M-token code-recall prompt | passes, 120.5 to 122.0 s | passes, 122.6 s |

All 28 production prefill engines have run factor 2 since 2026-10-10 18:08 UTC, and every one booted without OOM.

**This branch on GPU: not run.** The production numbers come from the same sizes on our build.

## Details

- **Why a config field.** The neighbouring sparse-MLA and indexer knobs (`sparse_mla_force_mqa`, `indexer_kv_dtype`, `hisparse_config`) live in `AttentionConfig`. `get_prefill_workspace_size` now takes the `VllmConfig`, like `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` already does.
- **Scope.** The FlashMLA workspace part applies to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a quantized DS-MLA cache. `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` also sizes the indexer in `deepseek_v2` (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x), `deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`, `hy_v4` and `glm5next`, so the factor applies there too. The DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA workspace is sized in `models/deepseek_v41` and does not read it.
- **Cost.** A step gathers in more passes only when its prefill requests hold more than `factor * max_model_len` context tokens in total. At the default above 256K (factor 2), that takes three or more concurrent near-full-length prefills.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs found with `gh pr list --state open --search` for "sparse prefill workspace", "prefill workspace size configurable", "flashmla sparse workspace", "indexer prefill buffer" and "workspace factor":
  - #42856 lowers the factors to 2 and 8 on SM120 only, stacked on #41834.
  - #60874 changes only the DeepSeek-V4.1 builders.
  - #59319 drops the reservation on the mixed-batch path. On the separate prefill path this knob still sizes it, and the two PRs touch one shared call line in `FlashMLASparseImpl.__init__`.
  - None makes the size configurable.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][weight loader] Stop warning when a parameter only widens the weight
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to [#51792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51792), which added this warning. `AutoWeightsLoader` emits it whenever a checkpoint weight's dtype differs from the parameter it lands in. A parameter declared wider than the checkpoint is a deliberate choice and the copy is exact, so that line reports nothing and buries the narrowing cases it was added for. Log the float widenings that cannot change a value at DEBUG instead of WARNING; every other mismatch still warns exactly as before.

## Claims

- A 48-layer Qwen3.x emits this warning 36 times at every start, once per linear-attention layer, for fp32 decay accumulators reading a bf16 `A_log` — counted from 180 occurrences over 5 starts in a serving log. All 36 are exact widenings, so the change is expected to log them at DEBUG instead; the post-change count was not measured on a model run.
- No other warning changes: the condition only subtracts from the cases that already fired.
- The conversions moved to DEBUG are exact for every finite input, not approximately: all 63,488 finite fp16 and 65,280 finite bf16 bit patterns round-trip through fp32 and fp64 unchanged, and fp32 round-trips through fp64.
- Nothing about loading changes — same values, same returned names. Only the level of the line changes; it is still logged, at DEBUG.
- Every other dtype mismatch still warns, including the fp8 pairs whose range looks wider but whose subnormals are shorter.

## Validation

On the branch point (`92044241a0`) and this PR, on CPU: load one parameter through `AutoWeightsLoader` for each stored → declared pair and record the level of the `Attempted to load weight` line.

| stored → declared | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bfloat16 → float32`, `float16 → float32`, `float32 → float64` | WARNING | DEBUG |
| `float32 → bfloat16`, `float16 → bfloat16` | WARNING | WARNING |
| `float8_e4m3fnuz → float8_e4m3fn` | WARNING | WARNING |

`pytest tests/models/test_utils.py`: 9 passed, the same tests as the branch point.

Exhaustive check of the pairs moved to DEBUG, run outside the suite: every finite fp16 and bf16 bit pattern cast to fp32 and to fp64 and back compares bit-identical, and none of them loses a value at `tiny/4`, `±max`, `1e-30` or `0.1`. Across the 8 float dtypes checked, 56 ordered pairs, the 5 widenings moved to DEBUG lose nothing at the probed values.

No model run, no multi-GPU, no performance measurement.

## Details

**Why a whitelist and not a predicate.** Comparing what the two formats hold reads as the general answer and is not. `eps`, `max` and `min` describe the normal range, so they miss the subnormal reach: `float8_e4m3fnuz` has the same 3 mantissa bits and a smaller `max` than `float8_e4m3fn`, which makes it look strictly narrower, but its exponent bias is one higher, 8 against 7, so its smallest subnormal is 2⁻¹⁰ against 2⁻⁹ and `0.0009765625` loads as `0.0`. A predicate built on those three fields calls that cast lossless and demotes a warning that matters. `torch.finfo` exposes no subnormal bound to repair it with, and the existing `is_lossless_cast()` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` compares `resolution`, `min` and `max`, and returns `True` for this very pair, so reusing it would carry the same gap. Listing the widenings that are exact by construction — fp16, bf16 or fp32 into fp32 or fp64 — is smaller and easier to verify at this scope.

**Relation to existing work.** [#51836](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51836) proposes config-driven changes to Qwen parameter dtypes, which is separate work on the parameters themselves; it is not landed, and it would need a config field present in each affected checkpoint. This PR changes the log level only: known-lossless widenings log at DEBUG instead of WARNING, every other dtype mismatch still warns, and no parameter or loaded value moves.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA] Cut ~21x host dispatch from the MLA metadata build
commits.pr_body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a host-dispatch microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the host build path, with per-call dispatch counts. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing host torch dispatches that serialize against the GPU on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency. Details under "End-to-end (side note)".

## Summary

Two spots on the MLA attention metadata build spend more time in PyTorch
dispatch than in the work they do. Both operate on tensors that are already
host-side and hold one entry per request, and both run on **every** build,
between decode steps.

### 1. `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`

Eight tensor dispatches — `sum()/item()`, a boolean-mask index, `numel()`,
`torch.all`, `eq`, `torch.nonzero`, `item()`, `torch.any` — to decide a single
integer. `qo_len` is derived from `query_start_loc_cpu`.

### 2. `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.build`, non-causal multi-token decode

A validation block using `torch.count_nonzero`, two `torch.all` calls and two
tensor-to-bool conversions (each lowering to `aten::is_nonzero`), purely to
raise a `ValueError` on a malformed query block.

Both now read the tensor out once and decide on Python ints.

## Results

Host cost, measured **without a GPU**. Both inputs are CPU tensors, so there is
no device work and no profiler involved in these numbers.

**`_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.88 µs | 0.32 µs | **5.9×** | 1.56 µs |
| 2 | 17.62 µs | 0.53 µs | **33.6×** | 17.10 µs |
| 8 | 17.65 µs | 0.71 µs | **24.8×** | 16.94 µs |

**non-causal query-block validation**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 11.88 µs | 0.84 µs | **14.1×** | 11.04 µs |
| 2 | 12.44 µs | 0.89 µs | **13.9×** | 11.55 µs |
| 8 | 12.58 µs | 1.20 µs | **10.5×** | 11.38 µs |

Combined at 2 requests: **30.06 µs → 1.42 µs, ~21×, 14 tensor dispatches
removed per build.**

The step from one request to two in the first table is the padded-CUDA-graph
case: with dummy rows present the function stops early-returning and runs the
full `nonzero`/`any` path, which is the shape a graph-captured decode hits.

## Why this path matters

On a Kimi-K3 conc=1 384K-context decode trace, all 8 GPUs are idle across the
metadata-build window between decode steps, so host time there is on the
critical path rather than overlapped. These two sites account for the
`count_nonzero`, `is_nonzero` and `eq`/`nonzero` operations visible in that
window.

## Correctness

No FLOPs change and no device work changes; both sites return small integers
and booleans.

- `_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`: **34067 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over
  every `qo_len` combination up to 4 requests × length 4 crossed with every
  plausible `num_decode_tokens`, plus 20000 randomised larger cases. Covers
  empty, all-zero, zero-interior, non-divisible totals, `uniform_qo_len <= 1`
  and trailing-zero inputs.
- non-causal validation: **21364 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over every
  query-length combination up to 5 requests × length 3, plus 20000 randomised
  cases, comparing all three returned predicates.

The `ValueError` text is unchanged: it now formats a list rather than calling
`.tolist()` on a tensor.

## Tests run

```
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
           vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py
All checks passed!

ruff format --check <same two files>
2 files already formatted
```

Equivalence harnesses were run inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` on CPU; output is
the case counts quoted above.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs before writing this:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "rocm_aiter_mla host"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "non-causal MLA uniform query block"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mla_attention count_nonzero"
```

Nearby open PRs (#57085, #57464, #54546, #58344) touch this area but none
addresses the host cost of these two functions.

## End-to-end (side note)

Deliberately last, and not the claim being made. End-to-end effect at this
operating point depends on how many metadata builds occur per step and on the
tuning of surrounding kernels, which is out of scope here. On our conc=1
Kimi-K3 configuration the expected effect is well under the run-to-run spread
we measure (~0.8%), so the function-level speedup above is the honest result.

---

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Opus 5). The measurements were
run by the submitter on MI355X hardware, and every changed line was reviewed by
the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Remove cascade attention
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove cascade attention from vLLM: its kernels, heuristics, metadata, scheduler/KV-cache plumbing, model-runner logic, config/flag handling, tests, and docs.

Cascade attention has been opt-in (`disable_cascade_attn=True` by default), already hard-disabled for FlashInfer (see #25679), force-disabled for async spec decode / DBO / batch invariance / CPU, and unsupported by most backends — yet it still costs a per-step scheduler scan, branches in the model runner and backends, and recurring bugs (#55674, #47183, #39208, #55227, #53690 are open fixes/workarounds that this PR makes moot).

**This PR is non-breaking for hardware plugins.** Plugin-facing APIs (`build(common_prefix_len, ...)`, `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks`, etc.) are kept as deprecated no-ops; a follow-up PR removes them once plugin maintainers have been notified.

## Claims

- No behavior change for default configurations (cascade was off by default); net **-901 lines in `vllm/`** (+504 / -1,405; most `+` lines are de-indentation in the FA/AITER forward paths after removing the cascade branch).
- The scheduler no longer scans the running request's blocks every step.
- Out-of-tree plugins keep working unchanged (checked against vllm-ascend, tpu-inference, vllm-gaudi, vllm-spyre, vllm-metal).
- `--disable-cascade-attn` / `disable_cascade_attn=` still parse; they warn and have no effect (to be removed in v0.33.0, same schedule as `--log-config-file`).

## Validation

**Accuracy** — GSM8K 5-shot, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, GB200, default backend:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0.5906 ± 0.0135 | 0.5345 ± 0.0137 |
| this PR | 0.5906 ± 0.0135 | 0.5345 ± 0.0137 |

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct,gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,max_model_len=4096 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto
```

**Shared-prefix batch** (the workload cascade targeted; same setup as the deleted `test_cascade_attention.py`): `Qwen/Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct`, >1K-token shared prefix, 64 identical greedy requests vs. 1 reference request → 64/64 identical outputs on both `FLASH_ATTN` and `FLASHINFER` (FlashInfer autotune disabled).

**Unit tests** — rows other than the last ran on the first commit (full removal); the second commit only re-adds the no-op shims, and the last row re-runs core suites on the final revision. (GB200; `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` for a local cubin version mismatch; writable `HF_HOME` for the sliding-window tests):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Scheduler / KV cache / prefix caching / cudagraph dispatch / arg utils / CPU platform / KV connectors / GPU model runner / mamba utils / simple KV offload | 923 passed, 22 failed — the same 22 fail identically on `main` here (`test_cpu.py` needs a CPU-only host; one PP test needs 3 GPUs; EC-connector priority tests) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py` | 151 passed, 7 skipped (incl. 18/18 sliding-window correctness) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k small` | 84 passed, 300 skipped |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k small` | 576 passed, 192 skipped |
| Other builder/runner suites (GDN, mamba2, linear, kpool, mm_prefix, trtllm, rocm selection, attn_utils, flex, prefix_prefill, kda, qsa, fusion) | 596 passed, 226 skipped, 42 failed — all 42 are `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention*`, which fail identically on `main` here (Triton `OutOfResources`: tensor memory 656 > 512 on GB200) |
| Compat-shim commit: scheduler / KV cache / runner / attention backends / builders | 996 passed, 84 skipped, 8 failed — all 8 also fail on `main` here (6 EC-connector priority tests; 2 PP tests needing more GPUs than the 1 visible) |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py tests/platforms/test_cpu.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_prefill_tail_classification.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k small
```
</details>

## Details

- **Config / CLI:** removed every place that read or force-set `disable_cascade_attn` (`VllmConfig` for async spec decode, batch invariance, DBO; `CpuPlatform`) and the "no piecewise cudagraph for cascade" warning.
- **Scheduler / KV cache:** the scheduler no longer computes common prefix blocks; `get_num_common_prefix_blocks` is removed from the coordinators and all single-type managers.
- **Model runner (V1):** removed `_compute_cascade_attn_prefix_len(s)`, cascade-driven FULL-cudagraph exclusion, and the cascade-only `num_sms` / `_init_device_properties`, `num_query_heads`, `use_alibi`. MRV2 never used cascade.
- **Backends:** removed `cascade_attention()` / `use_cascade_attention()` from FlashAttention (and diffkv), `MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper` from FlashInfer, and `use_cascade` / prefix–suffix metadata fields and branches from Triton, ROCm, ROCm AITER FA/unified, segmented, flex, CPU, and `CacheOnlyAttention`. `merge_attn_states` is unaffected (still covered by `test_merge_attn_states.py`).
- **Tests / docs:** deleted `test_cascade_flash_attn.py` and `test_cascade_attention.py` (and the system-message fixture/data only the latter used); updated `docs/design/cuda_graphs.md`.

**Kept as deprecated no-ops for out-of-tree plugins** (removed in a follow-up):

| API | Used by |
|---|---|
| `AttentionMetadataBuilder.build(common_prefix_len, ...)` (always 0) | ~20 vllm-ascend builders, tpu-inference, Cambricon, MetaX, Enflame |
| `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks` (now last field, defaults to `[]`) | vllm-ascend, tpu-inference, vllm-gaudi, vllm-spyre |
| `KVCacheManager.get_num_common_prefix_blocks()` (returns zeros) | vllm-ascend custom schedulers |
| `GPUModelRunner.cascade_attn_enabled = False`, `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding(use_cascade_attn=...)` (ignored) | vllm-ascend `NPUModelRunner` |
| `ModelConfig.disable_cascade_attn` (no effect) | vllm-ascend, vllm-metal |

**Known plugin impact:** the cascade fields of vLLM's attention metadata dataclasses (`use_cascade`, `common_prefix_len`, `cu_prefix_query_lens`, `prefix_kv_lens`, `suffix_kv_lens`, `prefix_scheduler_metadata`) are removed. Cambricon vllm-mlu's `MLUFlashAttentionMetadata(FlashAttentionMetadata)` passes them and will need to drop them when it moves to a release containing this PR (it currently tracks vLLM releases, not main). Enflame vllm-gcu pins `vllm==0.11.0` and is unaffected.

**Tradeoffs:** users who explicitly opted in with `--no-disable-cascade-attn` lose the heuristic-gated, FA-only cascade speedup for large shared-prefix batches. No new CPU/GPU syncs (the Triton/ROCm cascade paths' `seq_lens.cpu()` and FlashInfer's cascade-forced `seq_lens_cpu` requirement are gone). vllm-ascend's service-profiling config references `GPUModelRunner._compute_cascade_attn_prefix_lens`; that entry only matters when that profiler is enabled.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix TP group hang on steps without scheduled tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With a host pool shared across TP ranks (#56629), a TP group can hang forever on a step with no scheduled tokens. On such steps, every TP rank now waits at a CPU barrier right after its event wait.

## Claims

- Fixes a hang between TP rank 0 and a TP rank whose host is one step behind, on steps with no scheduled tokens (`no_forward`).
- Steps with tokens are unchanged.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** The script below copies the shared-event protocol from `hisparse/worker.py` onto 2 GPUs and holds rank 1's host for 0.5 s before one wait. Run on H100s:

```
torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py {zero_next|zero_now|tokens} {none|sync|barrier}
```

| Case | `main` (`none`) | rank 0 host sync (`sync`) | this PR (`barrier`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zero_next`: rank 1 late, next step has no tokens | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `zero_now`: rank 1 late on a step with no tokens, next step has tokens | HANG 3/3 | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `tokens`: rank 1 late, every step has tokens | PASS 3/3 | | |

When it hangs, GPU 0 is at 100% (spinning in the all-reduce) and GPU 1 is at 0% (its stream is blocked on the event).

**Unit test.** `test_zero_token_step_holds_tp_ranks_after_host_write_wait` checks that start_step waits at the TP barrier after the event wait on steps with no tokens, and only when the host region is shared.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -k "zero_token_step or draft_layer or full_graph_step or no_forward"
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` `worker.py` | 1 failed (`shared=True, num_tokens=0`), 7 passed |
| this PR | 8 passed |

These tests ran in a vLLM 0.31.0 H100 image (`f6d5a33`) with this branch's `worker.py` and test file swapped in. The image has no pytest, so a small runner expanded the parametrization. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

**Production.** A P/D decode deployment hit this hang. It runs HiSparse and NIXL through `MultiConnector`, at TP8 x DP4 with EP32 and MTP:
- One TP rank's GPU sat at 0% while its 7 TP peers sat at 100%.
- The other DP ranks then hit DeepEP dispatch timeouts.
- Each time, the engine was in its first minutes, when first contact with new prefill engines slows the NIXL read post on the main thread (0.1 to 2.4 s).

The reproducer shows the same GPU pattern. This patch has not yet run end to end on that deployment.

## Details

The protocol uses two shared events, A and B:
- Every step, each TP rank's stream waits on the event rank 0 recorded in the previous step.
- Rank 0 then records the other event in `finish_forward`.
- A stream wait binds to the most recent record at the time of the wait call.

**Trigger.** A TP rank's host falls one step behind rank 0, and the next step has no scheduled tokens.

**Mechanism:**

| | TP rank 0 | TP rank 1 (host late) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | step 5: wait A, launch forward 5, record B | still before its step 5 wait |
| 2 | step 6, no tokens: wait B, record A right away | |
| 3 | | step 5: wait A. The wait binds to rank 0's step 6 record |
| 4 | GPU: the forward 5 all-reduce waits for rank 1 | GPU: waits for the step 6 record, which is queued behind rank 0's forward 5 |

**Effect.** The TP group hangs and nothing times out. With DP and EP, the other DP ranks then block in their MoE collectives.

**Why steps with tokens are safe.** Before recording, rank 0 host-syncs on staging (`_finish_mirror_phase`). That staging is queued behind the previous forward's TP collectives, and every rank joins those only after its wait. A step with no tokens has no forward, so nothing orders rank 0's record after the other ranks' waits.

**Fix.** On steps with no tokens, every TP rank joins `get_tp_group().barrier()` (the CPU group) right after its wait. Every rank has then issued its wait before rank 0 can record again, on this step and the next.
- `num_tokens` comes from the same scheduler output on every TP rank, so all ranks take the barrier on the same steps.
- Without a shared host region, each rank uses its own local events, so there is no barrier.

**Why not a host sync on rank 0 alone.** The `zero_now` row: a sync can only prove that the other ranks reached the last step with a forward. A step with no tokens followed by a step with tokens still hangs.

**Cost.** One CPU barrier per step with no tokens. Those steps launch no forward.

**Not a duplicate.** I checked the 30 open PRs matching `hisparse`, plus searches for `host_write_event`, `hisparse hang`, `hisparse deadlock` and `hisparse barrier`. None changes how the shared host write events are ordered. #59877 fixes a separate NIXL thread-safety bug found in the same investigation.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, the change, the test and the reproducer.

<details>
<summary>hisparse_event_hang.py</summary>

```python
"""Two-rank model of HiSparse's shared host write events (hisparse/worker.py).

Rank 0 creates two IPC events and shares them. Every step, each rank flips to the
other event and its stream waits on the previous one (`start_step`). Rank 0 alone
records the current event at the end of the step (`finish_forward`), after a host
sync on staging queued before the step on steps with tokens (`_finish_mirror_phase`).
The forward is matmuls plus an all-reduce, standing in for the TP collectives.
Rank 1's host is held DELAY s before its step 5 wait.

  PLAN  zero_next  step 6 has no tokens
        zero_now   step 5 has no tokens, step 6 has tokens
        tokens     every step has tokens
  FIX   none       as on main
        sync       rank 0 also host-syncs before recording on steps without tokens
        barrier    every rank joins a CPU barrier after its wait on steps without tokens

torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py PLAN FIX [DELAY]
Prints PASS, or HANG with per-GPU utilization after 20 s.
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, threading, time

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

plan, fix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
delay = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0.5
zero_step = {"zero_next": 6, "zero_now": 5, "tokens": None}[plan]
assert fix in ("none", "sync", "barrier")
rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")
stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()

handles = [None]
if rank == 0:
    events = (torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True), torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True))
    for e in events:
        e.record(stream)
    handles = [tuple(e.ipc_handle() for e in events)]
dist.broadcast_object_list(handles, src=0)
if rank != 0:
    device = torch.device("cuda", rank)
    events = tuple(torch.cuda.Event.from_ipc_handle(device, h) for h in handles[0])
torch.cuda.synchronize()
dist.barrier()

done = threading.Event()


def watchdog():
    if not done.wait(20):
        util = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu", "--format=csv,noheader", "-i", "0,1"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        print(f"rank{rank} HANG at step {step}, GPU util: " + util.strip().replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        os._exit(2)


threading.Thread(target=watchdog, daemon=True).start()
a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
cur, nxt = events[1], 0
for step in range(10):
    has_tokens = step != zero_step
    staging = torch.cuda.Event()
    staging.record(stream)
    if rank == 1 and step == 5:
        time.sleep(delay)  # e.g. a slow NIXL read post before start_step
    prev, cur = cur, events[nxt]
    nxt ^= 1
    stream.wait_event(prev)
    if not has_tokens and fix == "barrier":
        dist.barrier(group=cpu_group)
    if has_tokens:
        y = a
        for _ in range(8):
            y = y @ a
            dist.all_reduce(y)
            y = y / 4096
    if rank == 0:
        if has_tokens or fix == "sync":
            staging.synchronize()
        cur.record(stream)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
done.set()
print(f"rank{rank} PASS", flush=True)
dist.destroy_process_group()
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Metrics] Count finished requests by watermark status
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `vllm:watermark_requests{status}`, a Prometheus counter of finished requests by watermark status. It exists only when `watermark_config` is set.

## Claims

- Each finished request gets exactly one status: `watermarked`, `skipped` or `not_watermarked`.
- `skipped` means the request asked for the watermark (omitted or `true`) but could not use it, such as `temperature=0` and trace replay requests.
- `not_watermarked` covers explicit opt-outs, pooling requests and internal requests (beam search steps, generative scoring, language detection).
- On an instance with `watermark_config`, the sum over `status` equals `vllm:request_success`. Both come from the same call in `IterationStats.update_from_finished_request()`.
- Without `watermark_config` the counter is not registered.

## Validation

Unit tests:

- `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`: requests of every status, including pooling, engine `ABORT`, `ERROR` and an `n=2` parent, finish through `OutputProcessor.process_outputs()` and are recorded by `PrometheusStatLogger`. The labels sum to `vllm:request_success`.
- `tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py`: the counter is registered only with `watermark_config`.

```
pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py
64 passed
```

E2E on H200 (`tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py`, now also checks the three labels and the sum for a watermarked, an opted-out and a `temperature=0` request):

```
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
1 passed
```

Manual scrape with `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --watermark-config '{"key": 42}'` after one watermarked, one `temperature=0` and one opted-out completion:

```
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="watermarked"} 1.0
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="skipped"} 1.0
vllm:watermark_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m",status="not_watermarked"} 1.0
vllm:request_success_total{engine="0",finished_reason="length",model_name="facebook/opt-125m"} 3.0
```

Without `--watermark-config`, `/metrics` has no `vllm:watermark_requests` series.

## Details

The status reads the same `SamplingParams` flags the GPU sampler reads: `watermarking`, and `_watermarking_skipped`, which the frontend sets when it resolves the request. `RequestState.from_new_request()` copies them into `RequestStateStats` once.

A request resolved again through the deprecated `EngineCoreRequest` path can carry both `_watermarking_skipped=True` and `watermarking=True`. It counts as `watermarked`, because `watermarked` is checked first.

The status is per request, not per token. A `watermarked` request can still contain tokens without the watermark (accepted draft tokens with `allow_target_only_watermarking`, repeated contexts with `deduplicate_contexts`, grammar-forced tokens). The docs list these cases.

Limitations, documented in `docs/features/watermarking.md`:

- In disaggregated prefill/decode, both instances count a request. Sum over decode instances only.
- For streaming input, the first input chunk sets the status.
- Client aborts are in neither counter, as with `vllm:request_success`.

Model Runner V1 cannot watermark, so there is no V1 path.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Add nightly Python 3.14 smoke test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

All CUDA CI runs on Python 3.12, so nothing checks the other versions `pyproject.toml` declares support for. This adds an optional (nightly) Buildkite step that installs vLLM into a Python 3.14 venv and runs a short generation.

## Claims

- `tests/standalone_tests/python_only_compile.sh` accepts `PYTHON_ONLY_COMPILE_PYTHON=<version>`. When set, it creates a uv venv with that interpreter, does the precompiled editable install into it with `uv pip`, asserts the interpreter version, and generates a few tokens with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`.
- With the variable unset, the script takes the same path as before.
- New step "Python 3.14 Smoke Nightly" in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`, next to "Python-only Installation", on the same `h200_18gb` device and `optional: true`.

## Validation

Run by hand on a B300 with CPython 3.14.5, not in the CI image:

- `uv venv --python 3.14` then `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto`: resolves and installs (torch 2.13.0+cu130), all compiled extensions import.
- The generation snippet added to the script passes on that venv with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, as the test image sets.
- The version assert fails when the expected version does not match the interpreter.
- `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` on the same venv answered chat, batched completions, JSON-schema structured output, a hermes tool call, and streaming.
- `pre-commit` passes on both files (including shellcheck and the Buildkite step-key and test-tethering hooks).

Not validated: the script end to end inside the test image, and the new step through the pipeline generator. The step needs to be unblocked on this PR to get that signal.

## Details

- The script already handles resolving the merge-base commit and waiting for its wheel on wheels.vllm.ai, so the new mode reuses it rather than adding a second script.
- This works without building anything because vLLM's extensions are `abi3`, and DeepGEMM ships per-version binaries for 3.10 to 3.14.
- Limitation: compiled code comes from the merge-base wheel, not the PR. The step covers the Python source and dependency resolution on 3.14, not C++ changes that break only on 3.14.
- Limitation: only the base install is covered. For example, `tensorizer==2.10.1` (the `tensorizer` extra and the test requirements) fails to import on 3.14 with a `KeyError`, which the `except ImportError` guard in `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/tensorizer.py` does not catch; this step would not see that.
- The wheel retry loop can wait up to 25 minutes, so the 30 minute timeout may need raising if the nightly regularly hits it.
- Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "python 3.14 CI smoke", "python_only_compile", and "3.14" in titles. The only hit is #51312, which is a torchao fix for the Rock image.

commits.pr_title: [Fix][Compile] Declare group_shape in the static FP8 quant fusion …
commits.pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9053
### Purpose
On recent torch (main, and the 2.15.0 RC from rc3), the fusion passes stop matching static per-tensor FP8 quant: RMSNormQuantFusionPass.matched_count == 0. CI shows it as All nodes remain for op _C::static_scaled_fp8_quant and rms_quant_fusion expected: [12], found: [0] (pytorch/test-infra#9053).

### Root cause

- QuantFP8 calls the static quant op with group_shape=[-1, -1] for per-tensor (input_quant_fp8.py). The shared pattern in MatcherQuantFP8 doesn't declare group_shape at all.
- Older torch matchers silently dropped any kwarg a pattern didn't declare, so this matched.
- pytorch/pytorch#199871 makes the matcher refuse a node that sets an undeclared kwarg to a non-default value, so a replacement can't silently lose it. pytorch/pytorch#200442 extends that check to auto_functionalized by reading the wrapped op's defaults.
- The schema default is group_shape=None, and the graph carries [-1, -1]. So even with #200442 the match is still refused.

### Fix
Declare group_shape in the static quant pattern, taken from the quant key: group_shape=[group_shape.row, group_shape.col]. That's the value QuantFP8 passes, and it's how rope_kvcache_fusion.py and qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py already write their static quant patterns. The pattern now states exactly what it matches, and it works with both old and new torch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all logprobs when completions requests logprobs=-1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`logprobs=-1` on `/v1/completions` means "return every logprob". The request validator accepts it explicitly (`completion/protocol.py:538-547` special-cases `-1` as valid) and `SamplingParams` expands it to the vocabulary size (`sampling_params.py:818-820`), so the engine computes full-vocabulary logprobs. But the serialization filter is purely `>=`-based:

```python
for i, top_lp in enumerate(step_top_logprobs.items())
if logprob_token_ids or num_output_top_logprobs >= i
```

With `num_output_top_logprobs == -1`, `-1 >= 0` is False, so the comprehension drops every candidate at every position. The client gets HTTP 200 with `logprobs.tokens` and `logprobs.token_logprobs` populated but `top_logprobs == [{}, {}, ...]` — silent data loss, after paying the full-vocabulary compute cost.

The chat handler already handles this correctly (`chat_completion/serving.py:1236-1238`):

```python
if return_all
or top_logprobs == -1
or (top_logprobs is not None and i < top_logprobs)
```

This applies the same rule to completions. One-line condition change plus regression coverage.

**Not a duplicate.** Per the duplicate-work checks in `AGENTS.md`:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "completion logprobs"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "top_logprobs"
gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "completions logprobs -1"
```

The nearest open PRs address different defects: #53722 guards a `KeyError` when the sampled token is missing from top logprobs; #47838 preserves logprobs when `top_logprobs` is *null*; #49320 handles an empty `logprob_token_ids` list. None touches the `-1` path. No open issue reports this.

**Existing coverage gap.** `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py::test_logprobs_minus_one_allowed` asserts only that the *request validator* accepts `-1` (`assert request.logprobs == -1`) — it never inspects the response. The chat side does assert the full-vocabulary result (`test_chat_echo.py:110-131`, `len(top_logprobs) == vocab_size`). That asymmetry is why this survived.

## Test Plan

The defect is in result serialization, so it is reachable without an engine, a model, or a GPU. `_create_completion_logprobs` reads only `self.return_tokens_as_token_ids`, so the test constructs the serving object via `__new__` — the same pattern `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py:625-640` already uses.

Added `test_completion_logprobs_honors_requested_count`, parametrized over `-1`, `1`, `2` against a three-candidate step, next to the existing `-1` validator test.

```bash
cd vllm
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
```

## Test Result

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
34 passed in 17.84s

$ .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <the two files above>
ruff check .......... Passed
ruff format ......... Passed
typos ............... Passed
(exit 0)
```

Negative control — reverting only `serving.py` and keeping the tests:

```text
>       assert len(logprobs.top_logprobs[0]) == expected
E       assert 0 == 3
1 failed, 2 passed
```

Only the `-1` case flips. The `1 → 2` and `2 → 3` cases pass both before and after, so the change is scoped to the broken path and does not alter the normal one.

**Model evals:** not applicable. This changes only how already-computed logprobs are serialized into the HTTP response; it does not touch sampling, the model, or generated token ids. No accuracy or serving-quality metric is affected.

**Environment note:** vLLM publishes no precompiled wheel for macOS arm64, so `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .` is unavailable on this machine. The tests above ran against the source tree in a `uv` venv with CPU torch and the transitive imports installed; they exercise pure-Python serialization and need no compiled kernels. Full-CI confirmation is welcome.

## Open question for maintainers

`logprobs=0` is handled inconsistently between the two endpoints, and I have deliberately **not** changed it here since it would alter existing behaviour:

| value | completions (`num_output_top_logprobs >= i`) | chat (`i < top_logprobs`) |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | keeps 1 candidate | keeps 0 candidates |
| `1` | keeps 2 | keeps 1 |
| `-1` | keeps 0 *(this PR: all)* | keeps all |

OpenAI's completions API documents `logprobs=n` as "the n most likely tokens", so completions returning `n + 1` looks off-by-one — but it is long-standing behaviour that clients may depend on, and `test_completion.py` has cases built around it. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if you would like it aligned.

---

*AI assistance was used for this change.* An agent located the defect by auditing the entrypoints package, drafted the fix and the tests, and ran the commands above. I reviewed every changed line, ran the test suite and the negative control myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Platform] Don't resolve current_platform during import vllm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #45424, `import vllm` resolves `current_platform` and loads platform plugins while vLLM is still half-imported, because `PIN_MEMORY` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` is computed at import time. This PR computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access, so `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform, as `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` requires. Same root cause as #48397; #48444 fixed only that issue's WSL symptom.

## Claims

- `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform. The resolver runs 0 times during `import vllm`, down from 1.
- An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`, directly or through another vLLM module, is detected again. Before this change it failed with `cannot import name ... from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`, and vLLM silently fell back to another platform.
- `PIN_MEMORY` keeps its value. All `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import PIN_MEMORY` sites and monkeypatches (e.g. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`) keep working.

## Validation

The existing dummy platform plugin's `register()` now imports a vLLM module, as real plugins do. A new subprocess test checks that `import vllm` leaves the platform unresolved and that the plugin platform still wins.

```bash
pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform
pytest -v tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py
```

| Check | main + new tests | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py`, CPU, rebased on current main | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| same, CUDA (L4)\* | 2 failed, 1 passed (`Expected DummyDevice, got cuda`) | 3 passed |
| resolver calls during `import vllm` (L4)\* | 1 | 0 |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (CPU) | 34 passed, 1 failed | 34 passed, 1 failed (same unrelated test) |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (L4)\* | — | 38 passed |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` greedy smoke run (L4)\* | — | OK, `PIN_MEMORY=True` on CUDA |

\* The L4 rows were run on an earlier base, 9dba339; I couldn't get GPU capacity to re-run them on current main. They also used an earlier version of the test, in which the dummy plugin imported `vllm.config`. On current main that import also runs into the separate `compilation.py` resolution described below, so the PR imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils` instead. The `torch_utils.py` change is identical, and no commits since 9dba339 touch `torch_utils.py`, `env_override.py`, `platform_utils.py` or `platforms/__init__.py`.

<details>
<summary>Fake out-of-tree plugin matrix (L4): 4 plugin styles × 4 first-import styles</summary>

**Plugin styles.** `register()` does one of:
- imports nothing;
- `import vllm.config`;
- `from vllm.config import VllmConfig`;
- nothing, but the platform module imports `vllm.config` at top level.

**First imports:** `import vllm`, `from vllm import LLM`, `EngineArgs`, `import vllm.config`.

| | cells not OK |
|---|---|
| main | 12/16 (plugin replaced by `NvmlCudaPlatform`, or `ImportError ... partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`) |
| this PR | 4/16 |
| before #45424 | 4/16 (same cells) |

The remaining 4 cells come from `vllm/config/compilation.py:22`, which resolves the platform during `import vllm.config`. That predates #45424 and is out of scope here.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main):
1. `vllm/__init__.py:14` imports `vllm.env_override`.
2. `vllm/env_override.py:153` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`.
3. `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py:76` runs `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()`.
4. `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py:45` imports `current_platform`, which resolves the platform and loads plugins.

This happens while `torch_utils` has only run up to line 76. A plugin that imports vLLM in `register()` gets an `ImportError`. Detection swallows it (`vllm/platforms/__init__.py`, `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`), so vLLM falls back to another platform and caches that platform's pin-memory setting.

**Fix.** A module `__getattr__` (PEP 562) computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access and stores it as a module global, so later reads are plain global lookups. The three uses inside `torch_utils.py` go through `_pin_memory()`, which also honours an assigned or monkeypatched `PIN_MEMORY`.

**Why the existing plugin test missed this.** The dummy plugin's `register()` imported nothing from vLLM, and the test only checks the final `device_name`. Also, the Plugin Tests CI step only triggers on changes under `vllm/plugins/` and `tests/plugins/`, so it did not run for #45424. It does run for this PR. Adding `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` / `vllm/env_override.py` to that step's `source_file_dependencies` would catch future regressions; I left it out to keep CI load unchanged, but can add it if maintainers prefer.

**Alternative considered.** Move `is_torch_equal*` out of `torch_utils`, so `env_override` no longer imports it (3 files, +68/-51). That also fixes `import vllm`, but it leaves the import-time platform resolution in `torch_utils` for the next early importer.

**Duplicate check.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `PIN_MEMORY`, `is_pin_memory_available`, `current_platform` + `import vllm`, `platform plugin circular import` and `partially initialized module torch_utils`. Only related, none open: #48397 / #48444 (WSL symptom of the same root cause) and #52285 (logging of detection failures).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write and test this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Serve LiquidAI/d1-3B on /v1/systemone
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve [`LiquidAI/d1-3B`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B) on `/v1/systemone` with answers that match the checkpoint's own `model.system_one()`, for text and image states.

The question types (#60696) and the `images` request field (#61064) have since landed on `main`, so this PR is now only the Liquid read strategy and the small changes to the next-token read that it needs.

```bash
vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B
```

## Demo

d1-3B playing Snake through `/v1/systemone`, recorded in real time on one B300. Each move is one HTTP request with a single `choice` question (up / down / left / right), and the snake takes the model's top choice with no fallback logic.

![d1-3B playing Snake on vLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/pr-60676-assets/d1_snake.gif)

In this 15 second run it made 666 moves (44 a second, 23 ms median per request), ate 46 apples and died once. The state is a short text: where the apple is relative to the head, and what is in each of the four neighboring cells. Given raw coordinates or an ASCII grid instead, the model played poorly (14 and 4 apples in 400 moves, against 32). The recording used the default prefix caching; see Details for why turning it off is faster here.

## Claims

- d1-3B picks and probabilities on `/v1/systemone` match the reference implementation shipped with the checkpoint, for text and image states and all three question types.
- Images are fetched once per request and shrunk to at most 1024 x 1024 pixels, as the reference does.
- A read that fails after rendering an image no longer breaks the next request that uses the same image.

## Validation

**Prompt parity (CPU).** For 15 questions over 11 cases, the rendered prompt and the label token ids are identical to what `prompt.py` in the d1-3B repo produces (`render` and `readout_ids`).

**Answers against the reference (one B300, bf16).** Reference: `AutoModel.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/d1-3B", trust_remote_code=True).system_one(...)` on transformers 5.18.0, each question asked alone. "Gap" is the largest absolute difference in any option's probability.

| Case | vLLM | Reference | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ticket, 3 questions (noul / choice / score) | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.0007 |
| Single choice | technical | technical | 0.0008 |
| Single noul | 0.018 | 0.020 | 0.0023 |
| Single score, 3 levels | 1.817 | 1.823 | 0.0032 |
| JSON state, 2 questions | billing / 0.349 | billing / 0.349 | < 0.0001 |
| Japanese text in a JSON state | Japanese | Japanese | 0.031 |
| Noul with criteria | 0.982 | 0.982 | < 0.0001 |
| Options named `a` to `d` | b | b | 0.0002 |
| Score, 10 levels | 7.373 | 7.373 | < 0.0001 |
| Image only (COCO 000000039769), 1 question | two | two | 0.0005 |
| Image and text, 2 questions | two / 0.984 | two / 0.986 | 0.0019 |

Every pick matches. The Japanese case has the same prompt tokens and the same pick; its distribution is spread over three options (0.33 / 0.51 / 0.16). I did not track down the source of that 0.031 gap.

**Reviewer findings (thanks @simon-veitner-redhat).** All five are addressed, re-implemented on the current `main` and re-checked on a B300:

| Finding | Now |
|---|---|
| A decision that fails after rendering an image breaks the next request with that image | Renders skip the sender cache. A failing two-question image request returns 400, and a chat request and a decision with the same image then return 200. |
| Each question fetches every image again | Images are fetched once and passed to every question. |
| Images above 1 MP differ from `system_one()` | Shrunk as the reference does. A 1280x960 image gives the same 1814 input tokens and probabilities within 0.0019. |
| A one-letter option name that is several tokens fails with a `max()` error | Returns 400 naming the label. |
| `confidence` differs from `system_one()` | Left as vLLM's definition. The docs now claim only picks and probabilities. |

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring
```

72 passed on a B300, on this branch as pushed.

**Not covered in CI.** There is no d1-3B end-to-end test, to avoid pulling a 3B checkpoint. The d1 prompt wording is pinned by a CPU-only unit test; the answer parity above was run by hand.

## Details

- **Why a strategy.** d1 is a post-trained LFM2.5-VL-3B that expects a fixed prompt (`QUESTION:` / `Options:` / `Reply with the option code only.`) and pools label variants (`yes`/`Yes`/`YES`, `A`/` A`). `LiquidStrategy` subclasses `NextTokenStrategy` and overrides only the user turn and the label tokens.
- **Label groups.** A read now takes a group of tokens per label and scores the best one. The generic strategy uses groups of one, so its behavior is unchanged.
- **Selected by architecture.** d1's `config.json` is the same as the base model's, so every `Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration` gets this prompt. Liquid's runner does the same.
- **Usage.** `input_tokens` sums the prompt of every question, so a multi-question request reports more than the reference, which counts the state once.
- **Limitations.** A `choice` is still capped at 26 options (the reference switches to two-digit codes beyond that). An empty-string state is treated like a `null` state.
- **Latency.** On one B300 a single-question request takes about 14 ms: roughly 9 ms in the engine step, 3 ms between the API server and the engine, and 1 ms each for HTTP and for rendering the prompt. With prefix caching on (the default) and a state that changes every request, the median rises to 22 ms and is bimodal (14 / 22 / 31 ms); `--no-enable-prefix-caching` brings it back to a flat 14 ms. I did not trace the cause in the scheduler.
- **Overlap.** Not a duplicate: no other open PR serves d1.
- **Shared changes.** The media connector moves from `JointSchemaStrategy` to the `ReadStrategy` base so both strategies use it, and every next-token render now skips the multimodal sender cache.

---

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Tidy `csrc/`: merge one-macro/one-function headers, rename the misnamed `attention/` dtype directory, move stragglers next to the extension that builds them, delete unreferenced code, and flatten `csrc/libtorch_stable/` back into `csrc/` now that nearly every GPU kernel is stable-ABI. No functional change intended.

Not a duplicate: the only open PR touching this area is #38134 (WIP, removes the KV cache dtype enum), which has a different goal and predates the `libtorch_stable/` layout.

## Claims

- `csrc/` is now `core/` (shared by every extension), `cpu/` and `rocm/` (legacy-ABI code), and everything else is the stable-ABI CUDA/HIP tree. `libtorch_stable/` is gone; extension names (`_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`) are unchanged.
- Every quoted `#include` resolves to the same file before and after the flatten (scripted over all 250 sources).
- The built CUDA extensions register the same 160 op schemas as `main`.
- Every `csrc/` path in the CI `source_file_dependencies` filters exists again. 68 entries had been left naming paths that moved under `libtorch_stable/`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CUDA build of `_C_stable_libtorch`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch`, `cumem_allocator`, `spinloop`, `fs_io_C` with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5 8.0 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0"` (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13) | builds and links |
| Registered op schemas vs. a build of `main` (`torch._C._jit_get_all_schemas()` after loading each `.so`) | identical, 160 schemas |
| Unified Marlin generator vs. the two old scripts, all archs | byte-identical output, 27 files each |
| x86 CPU extension (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, GCC 13) | every TU compiles except `cpu/utils.cpp` (missing system `numa.h` on the build box, file untouched here); not linked |
| ROCm | **not compiled** (no HIP toolchain). Ran torch's `hipify` on the old and new trees and checked that every quoted include of every HIP translation unit resolves after renaming |
| `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` | passes |

GPU kernel tests on an H200, run against the build of the first two commits (before the flatten):

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/core/test_{layernorm,activation,pos_encoding,fused_quant_layernorm,fused_silu_mul_block_quant,fused_qk_norm_rope,opcheck}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_{merge_attn_states,cache}.py`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py` | 6215 passed, 590 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{fp8_quant,fp8_quant_group,int8_quant,per_token_group_quant,cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm}.py` | all passed except `test_cutlass_subset` (see below) |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py` | 394 passed |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_w4a8,quant_op_schema,awq,gptq}.py` | 136 passed, 8 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,moe_permute_unpermute,grouped_topk,fused_topk}.py` | 2266 passed |

After the last commit (generator dedupe, folded files, `div_ceil`), rebuilt and re-ran the tests covering what it touched:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py` plus the Marlin cases of `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py` | 638 passed, 6 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{per_token_group_quant,int8_quant,fp8_quant_group}.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba`, `tests/kernels/test_{cache_kernels,concat_mla_q}.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py` | 2781 passed, 629 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_{cutlass_scaled_mm,machete_mm,cutlass_w4a8,block_fp8}.py` | 1375 passed, 108 skipped, 1 failed (`test_cutlass_subset`, see below) |

After the flatten commit, a fresh build directory builds and links for the same arch list with the same 160 op schemas, and:

| Tests | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_marlin_gemm.py`, `tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` | 624 passed, 264 skipped |
| `test_merge_attn_states.py`, `test_layernorm.py`, `test_fused_quant_layernorm.py`, `test_machete_mm.py`, `test_cutlass_w4a8.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba` | 5450 passed, 39 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_{moe_align_block_size,grouped_topk,moe}.py` | 2079 passed, 127 skipped |

`test_cutlass_scaled_mm.py::test_cutlass_subset` fails identically on a build of `main` on the same machine, so it is not caused by this PR.

Caveats on the local build: the machine has GCC 11.5, so the GCC ≥ 13 gate was bypassed in a scratch build dir and the DeepGEMM / DeepSelect / FlashMLA external projects were not built. ROCm and non-x86 CPU rely on CI.

## Details

**Layout**

```
csrc/
  core/             registration.h  scalar_type.hpp  cuda_compat.h
                    utils.hpp       (math.hpp + batch_invariant.hpp)
                    vec_dtypes/     (was attention/)
  cpu/              + ops.h, dynamic_4bit_int_moe_cpu.cpp
  rocm/             + dispatch_utils.h, quickreduce/
  attention/ moe/ quantization/ cutlass_extensions/ mamba/ gdn/ kimi_k3/
  *.cu, *.cuh, ops.h, torch_bindings.cpp   (was libtorch_stable/)
  cumem_allocator.*, fs_io.cpp, spinloop.cpp, *_registration.cpp
```

- `csrc/attention/` only held `Vec`/`FloatVec` dtype helpers. ROCm paged attention is the one place they are used for attention; elsewhere they are half/bf16/FP8 conversions. Hence `core/vec_dtypes/`.
- The legacy `_C` extension is ROCm-only and contains just quickreduce, so its bindings, kernel and headers live in `rocm/quickreduce/`. The op namespace (`_C_custom_ar`) is unchanged.
- The top-level `ops.h` only declared CPU ops (plus quickreduce), so it moved to `cpu/`.

**Removed as unreferenced**

- Files: `core/exception.hpp`, `cache.h`, `torch_utils.h`, `attention_utils.cuh`, `mamba/static_switch.h`, `cutlass_extensions/common.cpp`, the int8 `per_token_group_quant.cu` wrapper and its header, the second Marlin `generate_kernels.py`.
- Symbols: `VLLM_IMPLIES`, `Qk_dot`, `VLLM_SHFL_SYNC`, `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL_EXPAND`, `DEVICE_INLINE`/`HOST_INLINE`, the legacy `AT_*` dispatch macros other than `VLLM_DISPATCH_FP8_TYPES`, `cuda_utils::ceil_div` (now `div_ceil`), `TrivialEpilogue`, `identity`, `equivalent_cutlass_type`, `enable_sm120_only`, `barrier_at_start_release`, and the non-stable-ABI branches in two CUTLASS headers.

**Things reviewers may want to look at**

- `TORCH_UTILS_CHECK` is replaced by `STD_TORCH_CHECK`. The stable build already resolved to it; in the legacy-ABI `_rocm_C` extension an unsupported KV cache dtype string now raises `std::runtime_error` instead of `c10::Error`.
- `div_ceil` is `constexpr` without `__device__` and is now called from device code in `cache_kernels.cu`, which is also built for HIP.
- The CUTLASS include dirs and `CUTLASS_ENABLE_DIRECT_CUDA_DRIVER_CALL` were dropped from the ROCm-only `_C` target, which no longer includes CUTLASS headers.
- The flatten renames about 190 files, so open PRs touching `csrc/libtorch_stable/` will need a rebase (git follows the renames for edits; newly added files need moving by hand).
- CI: the filter commits change which jobs trigger. Also, quickreduce and the CPU `ops.h` now sit under `csrc/rocm/` and `csrc/cpu/`, which `ci_config.yaml` excludes from its run-all pattern, so changes to them only trigger jobs listing those paths.

**Out of scope**

- Grouping the loose kernel files at the `csrc/` top level into subdirectories.
- `get_device_attribute` in `cuda_utils_kernels.cu` caches its first result in a function-local `static` regardless of arguments, so the SM-count and max-shared-memory queries can return each other's value. Found while reviewing; it needs its own fix.
